rows.original: You realize that you’re a bit beyond the introductions, now that, well, now that you’re his Qal and you’ve already had sex, but for you and your kind, there’s a sort of ritual that goes on between two individuals looking for a longer-term relationship than a fling, and that’s called ‘dating.’ And a part of the process of ‘dating’ is learning more about each other. So, you ask [flurry.name] to tell you a bit more about his history: he’s lived a long time and he’s been all over the world in search of a mate. Surely he’s got some interesting stories to tell. [flurry.name] doesn’t answer at first: his head rotates slightly, like a confused dog seeing its own reflections, and you feel a light grip in your head as he scours your mind for some definitions. You are speaking the truth, he says, with a somewhat surprised tone to his voice. You’re the Qal. You ask if he didn’t believe you – if he thought you were lying. Not as such, he answers. This is not a ritual that my kind perform. All relevant information on the past is brought to the forefront upon courtship. Though, I suppose, your kind do not communicate as my kind do. [flurry.name] turns his head to face toward the central dome of the lair, where [frostwyrm.name] resides. He lets out a long sigh through his nose; you watch the steam shoot several feet before disappearing into the air. I was hatched a clutch of two, he begins. My bearer Qal joined the Grand Qim six Sky Cycles after my bearer Qim. As is typical for my kind, once our bearers joined the Grand Qim, we had left the nest in search of mates of our own. [flags.FLURRY_TALK_HISTORY |[flurry.name] mentioning his parents ‘joining the Grand Qim’ reminds you of the first time you asked him about how Frostwyrms deal with their dead, and what ‘joining the Grand Qim’ means... and how he reacted badly when you told him how [pc.race]s deal with their own dead. You opt not to repeat that mistake. | You tell [flurry.name] that [pc.race]s have a somewhat similar euphemism for death: you call it ‘passing away.’ You’re curious, though: when your kind die, you usually do anything from burning the remains to ashes, or burying the body under the ground, or some combination of both. Sometimes, someone might do something different. How do Frostwyrms handle the remains of those that ‘join the Grand Qim?’ Again, you feel [flurry.name] sift through your memories, search for multiple different words and phrases that you had just used. When he’s finished, he recoils slightly, as if you had just slapped him in the nose. This practice of yours is untenable! he balks. There is no equivalent to this heinous exercise among my kind, and for good reason! You truly mean to imply that your kind treat your fallen with such odious methods?! You suppose it can be seen as barbaric, in a sense, but, on the other hand, your kind reproduce significantly faster than Frostwyrms, and your lifespans aren’t nearly as long (generally). Your kind can’t just let the bodies stay there and pile up – you’d run out of places to put them in a hurry. You understand that it might be a sudden thing for someone like [flurry.name] to realize, but you ask him, as his Qal, to trust that different species have different approaches to different issues. [flurry.name] takes a moment to collect himself as he stews on your words. Eventually, he lowers his head back to the position it was before. As you say, he relents, although his voice comes out unsteady and unfocused. To answer your question... I am uncertain. The phrase ‘joining the Grand Qim’ is not a colloquialism: it is literal. The call occurs to us each individually, at different times; when one is summoned, they leave the nest and do not return. No one of my kind truly knows what becomes of one when they are summoned. How eerie – if that’s true, they don’t even leave bodies behind for their offspring to find and figure out what happened. ] The nest of my upbringing is a massive distance away – I had traveled so far and for so long that I do not believe I would be able to locate it again. I have since come across every manner of race and beast in search of a mate until I had met you and [frostwyrm.name]. There was no trace of any other of my kind until that day: when I found the coast she had made into her roosting grounds, her scent was faint, but unmistakable. [rand |You imagine him retelling every single fight he’s ever been in would take quite a while, given the scars on his body, and they might not be memories he’d be very keen to revisit. Instead, you ask him which fight was the most memorable, in whatever sense he’d prefer: whether because the fight was very close, or because his opponent was unique, or because of some other circumstance that made it stick with him. There is one, he says immediately, knowing exactly which fight he wants to talk about. A group of four individuals, standing on their hind legs[pc.isTaur | |, not unlike yourself ], each of them wielding a sharpened tool with a length longer than their bodies. There was one alpha among them: taller and stronger than the other two, and more familiar with its tool in combat. My territory was temporary, but it was well-marked, and I would not tarry intruders. You wonder what passes for a ‘well-marked’ territory for a Frostwyrm, if these three hunters ignored the signs completely. I must include that this encounter was recent, he continues. I had much combat experience to rely on by this point. My opponents were typically smaller in stature, but larger in number; I believed that I could quell this hunting group easily. Given that he’s still here, he clearly won the fight. The alpha of the three fought alone. It stepped forward, and with a heft, it flung its tool toward me. He lifts his right wing, unfurling it above you; he points to one particular scar along its leathery membranes with his snout. It’s not very wide, but judging by its color, that weapon pierced his wing all the way through. It struck true. Fortunately, I had grown accustomed to battle injuries; this one did not hinder my performance. [flags.FLURRY_VICTORY |You imagine [flurry.name] hasn’t actually lost any fights, given that, if he did, he’d probably be dead. Any fights, that is, save for you. How did this one individual stack up to you? As you say, my Qal: this alpha among them was inferior to your skill and knowledge. He hesitates before continuing. It was, however, my most difficult encounter before you. |You imagine that this ‘alpha’ must have put up quite the fight – or, at least, displayed quite the bravado, if they were willing to fight him one-on-one and after tossing their weapon at him. The alpha was, to date, the most difficult of my encounters, he confirms. And – now that I have a clutch and a nest of my own – my last, with any fortune. ] The alpha fought with a strength I was unready for; with a ferocity matched only by my own and with a cunning foretelling of a proud and proper Qal like yourself. They had strength enough to pry my jaw apart; they had speed enough to counter my every swipe; they were nimble and endurant enough to retaliate from a thrash of my tail after it had struck true. The alpha among the trio had time and again proven its mettle – I often consider the alternative reality of the two in its entourage joining the encounter, and how blessed I am that such a reality did not befall. [flurry.name] is really talking up whoever this opponent of his was. If the match was so even and deadlocked, how did he win? By chance, ultimately, he admits. A beat of my wing caused the cold dust to stir; the billows caught in the alpha’s eyes, and, whilst it was distracted, I lunged for its torso, sinking my jaws into its body and across its upper limb. The taste of its blood flooded my mouth and dripped from my maw, but I had no intention of earning my kill – once the tide of battle had shifted, its entourage sprang to action, and I took my gained opportunity to escape. [var0 |Wait a minute... a Frostwyrm, having fought an ‘alpha’ that stood on two legs and wielded a spear, and the Frostwyrm won by biting into its chest and arm, which would have left long, deep, repeating scars on their body.... That sounds like Edrei, the former alpha of Eitan’s tribe and Eitan’s own mother. [flurry.name] is the Frostwyrm that defeated her and forced her into retirement. You should... maybe keep this information to yourself. And hope that none of your Frostwyrm mates go poking around in your head about it. You wouldn’t want either [flurry.name] or Edrei to know that you’re friendly with their rival. Wow, though, |Wow, ]that’s quite the story! He was challenged to a one-versus-one by someone looking to pick a fight with Uveto’s apex predator, and they nearly won! Luckily for you and [flurry.name], though, he managed to get away with the win – even if it meant taking a deep stab wound in the wing for it. It has healed, he notes, flapping his wing once for effect. You’re attuned to the feelings and emotions coming from him via the psionic link, and you note that you don’t feel a twinge of pain... although, you suppose, for a psion like himself, he might just be blocking it. A victory is neither more nor less fantastic than any other, my Qal. Still, though... you and [frostwyrm.name] first became mates after she had beaten you in a fight (after you had beaten her a few times first, but who’s counting, really). There’s an alternate reality where [flurry.name] lost that fight... but there’s also another reality where he settled down with that alpha, just as [frostwyrm.name] had with you. |[flurry.name] has been alone this entire time, scouring the surface of Uveto in search of a mate before he finally found his way to you[frostwyrm.andNykke | and your own clutch | and [frostwyrm.name] ]. When you and [frostwyrm.name] first consummated, she said that she had ‘suffered innumerable heats and ruts,’ and that her ‘psionics had no bearing on the self.’ You imagine that [flurry.name] had a similarly difficult time trying to maintain his natural cycles without a mate. [flurry.name] stays still and silent for a long time. You hadn’t expected a negative reaction from him like this: all you said was he’s probably had a difficult, pent-up life without any way to deal with it. The truth, my Qal, is that... I.... Whatever’s bugging him is clearly pretty serious. You tell him that it’s okay; if he’s worried that you’re going to judge him, you won’t, and if he doesn’t want to speak any further, he doesn’t need to. [flurry.name] remains stoically silent for a time, although you can tell through your link with him that your words have an effect. My kind mate monogamously, he starts, and then stops again. Well... our circumstances are exceptional. But you already know and understand that. There was... one event. This happened fairly recently. I was perched lakeside some distance from the coast you and I had met on for some respite, when I noticed a... particular scent in the air. Something unfamiliar to me, and yet, instinctively alluring; intrinsically vital, somehow, to me and my very being. It was a faint scent, though the longer it lingered, the greater my base need to find it. A moment later, and there was a creature, [pc.isTaur |somewhat ]similar in stature to yourself, my Qal. It made garbled sounds; if it spoke a language like yours, though I have since forgotten the words. It approached me callously; as though I were intruding on its territory, yet my instinct wasn’t to strike, nor was it to retreat; my instinct... was to mate. To mate? That’s quite the leap, especially since he said that the creature looked [pc.isTaur |somewhat ]like you. When you and he first met, he was against the idea of mating anything other than another Frostwyrm and he had to be [flags.FLURRY_VICTORY |cajoled into |convinced to do ] it. After having consummated our mating pact with you and [frostwyrm.name], my Qal, I now understand the scent in the air to be that of another of my kind in the throes of their heat. I do not know how or why this smaller creature emitted such a fragrance. At that moment... I am ashamed to say that I lost control of myself. Mating was all I had the faculty to process. And so, I mated this small creature. With him doing the penetrating, right? It’s impressive to think that there’s someone or something else out there that’s capable of handling an entire Frostwyrm dick. At first, [flurry.name] doesn’t respond, so taken aback at your casual acceptance of the fact that he’s mated before he met with you. You feel tension through the psionic link as he readies himself for what he believes to be an emotional fallout, but it turns to relief when he begins to realize that you were earnest in what you said before: that you weren’t going to judge him for it. The creature continued to babble sounds through the act. I am unsure if it was trying to communicate with me, or to something else. The whole of my mind and body was focused on mating it, and my drive lasted for as long as the scent continued to linger in the air. I had seeded the creature multiple times before the scent – and the sensation – faded, and my senses returned to me. [flags.STEPH_DARGONED |Wait a minute... a creature, standing [pc.isTaur |somewhat ]like yourself; was awfully chatty the entire time; used pheromones to get a creature like [flurry.name] to behave irrationally horny; and is capable of taking a Frostwyrm’s dick, and therefore is likely to have had more than a few other insertions to practice with beforehand.... That sounds like Steph Irson, the famous, uh, conservationist that you see a lot on the viewports. Steph’s show, Steph Irson’s Galactic Huntress, is pretty famous for a handful of reasons – not the least of which is that she has lots of wild, raunchy sex with whatever topic creature she’s on about at the time. You even remember that episode of her having sex with a Frostwyrm. If you had known that this was ‘recent’ and not something she had taped long in advance, you could have tried to meet her and ask her where she found [flurry.name] – you and [frostwyrm.name] could have been more proactive in meeting him. Wait... if you can crossbreed with Frostwyrms, then shouldn’t she be able to, as well? Well, best not to worry about it too much, now. The guilt of mating before being mates still clearly weighs on [flurry.name]’s mind, even if he wasn’t totally in control of himself at the time, and he’s not so keen to keep thinking about it. Hopefully Steph considers herself lucky that [flurry.name] was so adamant about finding another Frostwyrm to mate with. Being betrothed to a dragon would really cut into her creative prospects... but, probably, not her ratings. |You can feel through the psionic link that, despite your assurances, the guilt of mating before he’s found a mate still weighs on [flurry.name]’s consciousness, and he isn’t too keen on talking some more about it. Still, though, that’s a wild story: not only did he get a brief reprieve from his intense ruts without a partner to sate them with, but he did it with someone like you – someone small, bipedal, and very-much-not-a-Frostwyrm. It’s wild and interesting to think that there’s someone else out there that had an encounter with a Frostwyrm like you did, and so recently, too! In a way, you feel a bit sad that whoever [flurry.name] mated with caught him when he was so adamant that he find another Frostwyrm to mate with. In your experience, Frostwyrms make amazing mates, lovers, and partners. ] ]
rows.translation: 你意识到，现在才互相介绍已经有些晚了，毕竟，呃，毕竟你已经是他的Qal，而且你们也已经做过爱；但对你和你的族人来说，两个想要建立比露水情缘更加长久关系的人之间，会进行某种名为‘约会’的仪式。而‘约会’过程的一部分，就是更加了解彼此。因此，你请[flurry.name]多讲一点他的过去：他已经活了很久，也曾走遍世界各地寻找伴侣。想必他有不少有趣的故事可讲。 [flurry.name]起初没有回答：他的脑袋微微转动，就像一条困惑的狗看见自己的倒影；当他在你的脑海中搜寻某些定义时，你感觉脑中被轻轻握住。你说的是真话，他说道，声音里带着几分惊讶。 你可是Qal。你问他是不是不相信你 – 是不是以为你在撒谎。 并非如此，他回答。我的种族并不举行这种仪式。求偶时，一切与过往有关的重要信息都会被置于意识最前沿。不过，我想你们的种族并不像我的种族这样交流。 [flurry.name]转过头，望向巢穴中央的穹顶，[frostwyrm.name]就住在那里。他从鼻中长长叹出一口气；你看着蒸汽喷出数英尺，随后消散在空气中。我与另一只幼崽同窝孵化，他开始说道。生育我的Qal在生育我的Qim之后六个天空周期加入了伟大Qim。正如我族通常所做的那样，在我们的生育者加入伟大Qim之后，我们离开巢穴，各自寻找自己的伴侣。 [flags.FLURRY_TALK_HISTORY |[flurry.name]提到他的双亲‘加入伟大Qim’，让你想起第一次询问霜龙如何处置死者、‘加入伟大Qim’又是什么意思时的情形...以及当你告诉他[pc.race]如何处理自己的死者时，他反应得有多糟。你决定不再犯同样的错误。 | 你告诉[flurry.name]，[pc.race]对死亡也有一种颇为相似的委婉说法：你们称其为‘离世。’不过，你很好奇：你的族人死后，通常会把遗骸焚烧成灰，或将尸体埋入地下，又或是两者结合。有时，也会有人采取不同的做法。霜龙会如何处理那些‘加入伟大Qim’者的遗骸？ 你再次感觉到[flurry.name]翻检你的记忆，搜寻你刚才使用的好几个不同词语和短句。等他结束后，他微微后缩，仿佛你刚才扇了他的鼻子一巴掌。你们这种做法不可容忍！他惊斥道。我的种族中没有任何与这种恶行相当的做法，而且这是有充分理由的！你真的是说，你的种族竟会用如此可憎的方式对待死者？！ 你觉得，从某种意义上说，这或许会显得野蛮；但另一方面，你的族人繁殖速度远快于霜龙，寿命也远没有他们漫长（通常如此）。你的族人不可能任由尸体留在原地堆积 – 那样很快就会无处安放。你明白，对[flurry.name]这样的人而言，这或许是个突如其来的认知；但你以他的Qal身份请他相信，不同种族会以不同方法应对不同问题。 [flurry.name]琢磨着你的话，花了片刻让自己镇定下来。最终，他把头重新低回原来的位置。如你所言，他让步道，尽管声音听起来仍不稳定，思绪也有些涣散。回答你的问题...我并不确定。‘加入伟大Qim’这句话并非俗语：它指的是字面意义。召唤会在不同时间分别降临到我们每个人身上；当某人受到召唤，他们便会离开巢穴，再也不回来。我的族人没有谁真正知道，被召唤者最后会变成什么。 真是诡异 – 如果这是真的，他们甚至不会留下尸体，让后代找到并弄清发生了什么。 ] 养育我的巢穴在极其遥远的地方 – 我旅行得太远、太久，已经不觉得自己还能再次找到它。此后，我为了寻找伴侣，遇到过各种各样的种族与野兽，直到遇见你和[frostwyrm.name]。在那天之前，我从未发现过任何其他同族的踪迹：当我找到她用作栖息地的那片海岸时，她的气味虽然微弱，却绝不会认错。 [rand |看他身上的累累伤疤，你猜，如果让他复述自己经历过的每一场战斗，恐怕会花上相当长时间，而且那些记忆或许也不是他很愿意重温的。于是，你问他哪一场战斗最令他难忘，至于是哪种意义上的难忘，则由他决定：或许是因为战况非常胶着，或许是因为对手十分独特，又或许是因为某种其他状况使那场战斗铭刻在他的记忆里。 确实有一场，他立刻说道，显然十分清楚自己想谈哪一场战斗。那是一群由四个个体组成的队伍，他们用后腿直立[pc.isTaur | |，与你并无不同 ]，每一个都挥舞着一件经过磨利、长度超过其身体的工具。他们之中有一个首领：比另外两个更高、更强，也更熟悉如何在战斗中使用它的工具。我的领地虽然只是暂时的，却有清楚的标记，而我不会容忍入侵者逗留。 既然这三个猎人完全无视了那些标志，你不禁好奇，怎样的领地对霜龙来说才算‘标记清楚。’ 我必须补充一点，这次遭遇发生在不久之前，他继续说道。那时，我已经积累了丰富的战斗经验可供依仗。我的对手通常体型较小，数量却更多；我以为自己可以轻易制服这支狩猎队。 既然他现在还在这里，那显然是他赢了。 三者之中的首领独自战斗。它走上前来，用力一掷，把手中的工具投向了我。他抬起右翼，在你上方舒展开来；他用吻部指向翼膜上的一道特定伤疤。伤口并不很宽，但从颜色判断，那件武器彻底贯穿了他的翅膀。它准确命中了。幸运的是，我已经习惯了战斗造成的伤势；这一处并未影响我的表现。 [flags.FLURRY_VICTORY |你猜[flurry.name]实际上从没输过任何战斗，毕竟，如果他输过，恐怕早就死了。任何战斗都是如此，除了与你的那一场。那么，这一个对手和你相比如何？ 正如你所说，我的Qal：他们之中的这个首领，无论技巧还是知识都不如你。他犹豫片刻，才继续说道。不过，在遇见你之前，这是我经历过最艰难的一战。 |你猜这个‘首领’一定进行了相当激烈的抵抗 – 或者，至少表现出了相当惊人的勇气，毕竟对方不仅愿意和他单打独斗，还先把自己的武器投了出去。 直至今日，那名首领仍是我遇到过最难对付的对手，他证实道。而且 – 既然我如今已有自己的后代和巢穴 – 如果幸运的话，那也是最后一个。 ]那名首领展现出的力量令我措手不及；其凶猛唯有我自己能够匹敌，其机敏则预示着它会成为如你一般骄傲而合格的Qal。对方力气大到足以掰开我的上下颚；速度快到足以化解我的每一次挥击；也足够灵活坚韧，能在被我的尾巴结结实实抽中后立刻反击。三者之中的首领一再证明了自己的勇武 – 我常常设想，如果它身边的两个同伴也加入战斗，事情会变成什么样，并庆幸那种现实并未降临到我身上。 [flurry.name]对这名对手真是赞不绝口。如果战斗如此势均力敌、僵持不下，他最后是怎么赢的？ 归根结底，是靠运气，他承认道。我的翅膀一次拍动，扬起了冰冷的粉尘；翻涌的尘雾扑入首领眼中，趁对方分神时，我猛扑向它的躯干，一口咬住了它的身体和上肢。它的血味灌满我的口腔，从我的血盆大口中滴落，但我无意夺取这份猎杀成果 – 当战局发生逆转后，它的同伴立刻采取行动，而我则利用刚刚赢得的机会逃离。 [var0 |等一下...一条霜龙，曾经和一个双腿直立、挥舞长矛的‘首领’战斗，而霜龙靠咬住对方的胸膛与手臂取得胜利，这应该会在其身上留下又长又深、成排分布的伤疤.... 听起来像是埃德蕾，埃坦部族的前任首领，也是埃坦的亲生母亲。[flurry.name]就是击败她、迫使她退隐的那条霜龙。 你应该...也许最好把这个消息藏在心里。还要希望你的霜龙伴侣都不要为了这件事翻查你的脑袋。你可不希望[flurry.name]或埃德蕾的任何一方知道，你与他们的对手关系友好。 不过，哇， |哇， ]这故事可真精彩！有个想找乌维托顶级掠食者打架的人，向他发起了一对一挑战，而且对方险些赢了！不过你和[flurry.name]很幸运，他最终还是成功取胜并脱身 – 哪怕为此被人在翅膀上刺出了一道很深的伤口。 它已经痊愈了，他指出，同时拍了一下翅膀作为展示。你通过灵能连接，敏锐感受着他传来的感觉与情绪，并注意到自己没有察觉任何疼痛的抽动...不过，你想，对于他这样的灵能者而言，或许只是把痛楚屏蔽掉了。一场胜利和任何其他胜利相比，既不会更令人惊叹，也不会稍逊一筹，我的Qal。 不过嘛...你和[frostwyrm.name]最初是在她战胜你之后结为伴侣的（在那之前你先赢过她几次，但说真的，谁会计较呢）。存在着另一个现实，[flurry.name]输掉了那场战斗...但也存在另一个现实，他像[frostwyrm.name]与你安定下来一样，和那名首领结成了伴侣。 |[flurry.name]此前一直孤身一人，为了寻找伴侣而踏遍乌维托地表，最后才终于找到了你[frostwyrm.andNykke |和你自己的后代 |以及[frostwyrm.name] ]。你和[frostwyrm.name]第一次完成交配时，她说自己曾‘经受过无数次发情与求偶期’，还说她的‘灵能对自身不起作用。’你猜[flurry.name]在没有伴侣的情况下，试图熬过自己的自然周期时，也经历了同样艰难的时光。 [flurry.name]一动不动地沉默了许久。你没料到他会有这样负面的反应：你只是说，没有任何方式可以发泄，他的人生大概过得很艰难、很压抑。 真相是，我的Qal，我...我.... 困扰他的事情显然非常严重。你告诉他没关系；如果他担心你会评判他，你不会这么做；如果他不想继续说下去，那也不必勉强。 [flurry.name]又以坚忍的沉默维持了一段时间，不过你能通过彼此的连接看出，你的话对他产生了影响。我的种族实行单偶制，他开口，却又停了下来。好吧...我们的情况很特殊。但你已经知道，也已经理解这一点。 曾经发生过...一件事。事情就在不久之前。当时，我栖息在一座湖边休息，距离你我相遇的那片海岸颇有一段路；就在这时，我注意到空气里有一种...特殊的气味。那是我不熟悉的东西，却又本能地令我着迷；不知为何，对于我和我的存在本身而言，它从本质上显得至关重要。那股气味十分微弱，但它萦绕得越久，我寻找其来源的原始需求就越强烈。 片刻后，那里出现了一个生物，我的Qal，其体态[pc.isTaur |有几分 ]与你相似。它发出含混不清的声音；如果它说的是与你类似的语言，那些词语我此后也已经忘记。它毫无顾忌地接近我；仿佛是我侵入了它的领地，可我的本能既不是出击，也不是撤退；我的本能...是交配。 交配？这跳跃可真够大的，尤其是他说那个生物看起来[pc.isTaur |有几分 ]像你。你和他第一次见面时，他还反对与霜龙以外的任何生物交配，而且你不得不[flags.FLURRY_VICTORY |连哄带劝地让他接受 |说服他去做 ]这件事。 在我们与你和[frostwyrm.name]完成交配契约之后，我的Qal，我现在才明白，当时空气中的气味来自另一个正处于发情高潮的同族。我不知道这个较小的生物为何或如何散发出这样的芳香。在那一刻...我羞于承认，自己完全失去了控制。我的心智只能理解交配这一件事。所以，我与这个小生物交配了。 是他负责插入，对吧？想到外面还有某个人或某种生物能容下整根霜龙肉棒，实在令人印象深刻。 起初，[flurry.name]没有回应；他对你如此坦然地接受他在与你相遇之前曾和别人交配过这一事实感到万分惊讶。你透过灵能连接感到他全身紧绷，为自己以为即将到来的情绪爆发做好准备；但当他逐渐意识到你先前说的确实出自真心，也就是你不会因此评判他，那份紧张便化作了宽慰。 在整个过程中，那生物都在不断发出含混的声音。我不确定它是在尝试与我交流，还是在和别的什么东西交流。我的整个心智与身体都专注于和它交配，而只要那股气味仍在空气中萦绕，我的欲望就始终不曾消退。在那股气味 – 以及那种感受 – 消散、我的理智重新回归之前，我已经让那生物受精了好几次。 [flags.STEPH_DARGONED |等一下...一个[pc.isTaur |有几分 ]像你一样直立的生物；整个过程中话多得出奇；会使用信息素让[flurry.name]这样的生物变得毫无理智地饥渴；而且还能容下霜龙的肉棒，因此很可能事先已经经历过不止几次插入，以此积累经验.... 听起来像是斯蒂芬·厄森，那个大名鼎鼎的，呃，保育人士，你经常能在视讯屏幕上看见她。斯蒂芬的节目《斯蒂芬·厄森的银河女猎手》因为好几个原因而非常出名 – 其中绝对少不了她会和当期介绍的任何生物进行大量狂野淫荡的性爱。你甚至记得她与一条霜龙做爱的那一集。如果你早知道这件事发生在‘不久前’，而不是她提前很久录好的内容，你本可以尝试与她见面，问问她在哪里找到了[flurry.name] – 你和[frostwyrm.name]本可以更主动地去见他。 等等...如果你能和霜龙杂交，那她不是也应该可以吗？ 好吧，现在最好别太担心这件事。尽管当时他并不完全能控制自己，但在成为伴侣之前与别人交配的罪恶感显然仍在压着[flurry.name]的心头，他也并不愿继续思考这件事。 希望斯蒂芬会因为[flurry.name]当时坚持要找另一条霜龙交配而庆幸自己幸运。和一条龙订婚，实在会大大限制她的创作前景...不过，大概不会影响她的收视率。 |你能透过灵能连接感觉到，尽管你一再保证，在找到伴侣之前便和别人交配的罪恶感仍然压在[flurry.name]的意识上，而他并不愿继续谈论这件事。 不过，这故事仍然相当疯狂：他不仅得以短暂摆脱没有伴侣满足需求时的强烈求偶冲动，而且还是和像你一样的某个人做到的 – 一个体型娇小、双足直立、彻彻底底不是霜龙的人。想到外面还有另一个人也像你一样遇到过霜龙，而且就在不久之前，实在既疯狂又有趣！ 从某种意义上说，你有点遗憾：不论[flurry.name]交配的对象是谁，对方遇见他时，他都还坚定地只想寻找另一条霜龙交配。根据你的经验，霜龙是棒极了的伴侣、爱人和人生伙伴。 ] ]
rows.raw: " You realize that you’re a bit beyond the introductions, now that, well, now that you’re his Qal and you’ve already had sex, but for you and your kind, there’s a sort of ritual that goes on between two individuals looking for a longer-term relationship than a fling, and that’s called ‘dating.’ And a part of the process of ‘dating’ is learning more about each other. So, you ask [flurry.name] to tell you a bit more about his history: he’s lived a long time and he’s been all over the world in search of a mate. Surely he’s got some interesting stories to tell. [flurry.name] doesn’t answer at first: his head rotates slightly, like a confused dog seeing its own reflections, and you feel a light grip in your head as he scours your mind for some definitions. You are speaking the truth, he says, with a somewhat surprised tone to his voice. You’re the Qal. You ask if he didn’t believe you – if he thought you were lying. Not as such, he answers. This is not a ritual that my kind perform. All relevant information on the past is brought to the forefront upon courtship. Though, I suppose, your kind do not communicate as my kind do. [flurry.name] turns his head to face toward the central dome of the lair, where [frostwyrm.name] resides. He lets out a long sigh through his nose; you watch the steam shoot several feet before disappearing into the air. I was hatched a clutch of two, he begins. My bearer Qal joined the Grand Qim six Sky Cycles after my bearer Qim. As is typical for my kind, once our bearers joined the Grand Qim, we had left the nest in search of mates of our own. [flags.FLURRY_TALK_HISTORY |[flurry.name] mentioning his parents ‘joining the Grand Qim’ reminds you of the first time you asked him about how Frostwyrms deal with their dead, and what ‘joining the Grand Qim’ means... and how he reacted badly when you told him how [pc.race]s deal with their own dead. You opt not to repeat that mistake. | You tell [flurry.name] that [pc.race]s have a somewhat similar euphemism for death: you call it ‘passing away.’ You’re curious, though: when your kind die, you usually do anything from burning the remains to ashes, or burying the body under the ground, or some combination of both. Sometimes, someone might do something different. How do Frostwyrms handle the remains of those that ‘join the Grand Qim?’ Again, you feel [flurry.name] sift through your memories, search for multiple different words and phrases that you had just used. When he’s finished, he recoils slightly, as if you had just slapped him in the nose. This practice of yours is untenable! he balks. There is no equivalent to this heinous exercise among my kind, and for good reason! You truly mean to imply that your kind treat your fallen with such odious methods?! You suppose it can be seen as barbaric, in a sense, but, on the other hand, your kind reproduce significantly faster than Frostwyrms, and your lifespans aren’t nearly as long (generally). Your kind can’t just let the bodies stay there and pile up – you’d run out of places to put them in a hurry. You understand that it might be a sudden thing for someone like [flurry.name] to realize, but you ask him, as his Qal, to trust that different species have different approaches to different issues. His instincts are still trying to parse how it’s even possible. But you have every belief that he’s going to be just as attentive a Qim to this kip as he has been to his clutch so far. ] Now that [var5|both eggs have|the egg has] been laid, it’ll be four more months until [var5|they’re|the egg is] ready to hatch, and then another four for it to mature. The kip inside it will incubate in all that time, but unless both parents – the Qim and the Qal – are present, the baby will simply never hatch. It’ll stay inside the egg until you’re both ready. You’ve already spent four months here with [flurry.name] and [frostwyrm.andNykke |the rest of your draconic family |[frostwyrm.name] ]; what’s another eight?

rows.raw: " The first four months of [var1 |[flurry.name] |[frostwyrm.name] ]’s pregnancy[var5| – and your own –] go by in a hurry. Although you may be the Qal of the clutch, you still aren’t a [pc.ra frostwyrm |pureblood ]Frostwyrm; you rely on [frostwyrm.name][frostwyrm.andNykke |, Nykke, ] and [flurry.name] for food and warmth. Not that you often need the latter: the lair is surprisingly well insulated for a place that’s made entirely of ice and snow, and there’s more than enough body heat to spare between [frostwyrm.andNykke |all of ]your draconic lovers. Each night ends with you being wrapped up in between [frostwyrm.andNykke |three |two ] slumbering dragons, snuggling up tightly against you with you between them. It takes about two months for [var1 |[flurry.name] |[frostwyrm.name] ]’s body to show any significant difference, and even then, it’s not much: Frostwyrm eggs are about the size of a normal human baby when they’re laid, and Frostwyrm biology is large enough that they can support something that comparatively small with ease. The biggest outward difference is that [flurry.name]’s belly gets a little firmer, and he doesn’t look like he put on some weight so much as it looks like he just had a little bit too much to eat.[var5 | You, on the other hand, don’t get off nearly so lightly. By the end of the second month, your stomach has rounded out noticeably, and your walk across the lair slowly turns into a waddle. Life isn’t any more difficult – your dragons won’t let it be – but it does get a little more awkward. The kip inside you is capable of some rudimentary psionics, broadcasting raw, unfocused emotions at random; every so often, they stutter and overlap with the ones coming from [flurry.name]’s egg, and he assures you that the two kips are simply ‘speaking’ to each other in the only way they know how. By the end of the fourth month, getting up and lying down has become a chore, and you spend most of your days curled against [flurry.name]’s side while his psionics dull the worst of your aches. ] Another two months later, and, right on schedule, the egg’s gestation period ends: [var1 |[flurry.name] was keeping himself entertained by scouting different parts of the lair and grinding his horns against one of the rougher walls to smoothen both, when, suddenly, it happens. You feel through your psionic link with him that the egg is ready before he has a chance to enunciate it to anyone. He’s |[frostwyrm.name] was keeping herself busy with playfully swatting and nuzzling against her other kips, when, suddenly, it happens. You feel through your psionic link with her that the egg is ready before she has a chance to enunciate it to anyone. She’s ] gently lead back to [var1 |his |her ] normal resting spot where [var1 |he |she ] passes the egg easily and without complications, and, after a thorough cleaning, you’re left with a normal, healthy Frostwyrm egg.[var5 | You aren’t far behind. Not long after, you feel an awkward jerk deep inside your womb, followed by the instinctive need to push. Thankfully, the egg isn’t any larger than a typical [pc.race] baby, and its smooth shell makes it easier to pass than you had feared – though it’s still far from easy. [flurry.name] stays curled around you the whole time, blocking the pain from your mind, and by the end of the ordeal, there are two oblong Frostwyrm eggs resting side by side in the lair. ][var3 |[var2 | After laying the egg, [flurry.name]’s whole attention is devoted strictly to it: everything from the exact position it’s in as it lies on its side, incubating safely beneath him, to counting the seconds it’s left in the air when he needs to get up for any reason. You sometimes catch him staring at it, with his chin resting against the floor. The emotion you feel from him is... powerful. It’s not just love or adoration; it’s something else. His entire life was devoted to this moment: to finding a mate and laying his first kip, and now, after going so long without a mate and having escaped so many fights with his life just to get to this moment... it’s here. Inside that egg is a real kip. His kip. It’s not an emotion that can be adequately put to words. | [flurry.name]’s actions and reactions to having laid the egg, while still as devoted and attentive as ever, are nonetheless... a bit muted, at least compared to the first egg you two ever had. Before, he would count the seconds the egg was left alone whenever he needed to leave for something, such as food; now, he simply tucks the egg into a thin layer of ice shavings and considers it protected well enough that he can relax when he needs to leave. It reminds you somewhat of how [pc.ra frostwyrm |[pc.originalRace] |[pc.race] ]’s react to having multiple kids: with the first one, people tend to overreact to how fragile the kids are and how much attention they need at all times, but by the second, they’re experienced enough to know that, well, in [flurry.name]’s case, the egg isn’t going to crack just because he didn’t look at it long enough or something. That’s not to say he takes his duties as the Qim any less seriously: every moment he’s in the lair, his focus is on the egg and ensuring that the kip inside it is comfortable to the best of his ability. It just means that he’s allowing himself to relax a little more often. ] ][var0 | As is usual, [frostwyrm.name]’s demeanor changes once the egg is hatched: although her posture and attitude towards you is just as bright and loving as ever, she is nonetheless instinctually protective of the egg and broods atop it for most hours of the day, often forgoing food until she’s starving, and even then, when she gets up to feed herself, you can tell that she’s a bit uncomfortable about it. Although this isn’t new for her, it’s nonetheless... different. This is her kip that she’s incubating, but it’s also one for the next generation of pureblood Frostwyrms in Uveto. She broods it like she does any other egg she’s laid, but she, and you, and [flurry.name] know that it’s not quite the same. Her species depends on this kip hatching and developing into a healthy Frostwyrm. That’s not to say that she considers this kip to be any ‘more important’ than her current clutch. And the fact that its sire was not her Qal always leaves room for uncertainty, no matter how certain you both are. ][var4 | While this isn’t the first kip that [flurry.name]’s ever had, he nonetheless acts differently around it. rows.original: The egg may be laid, but it’s not yet hatched – you can’t rightly say you’ve added another kip to your clutch until it has. While it’s not about to hatch without you here, you’re still not going to miss any bit of it for the world. The first month of the egg incubation was admittedly rather boring. [var3 |Neither you nor [flurry.name] are pregnant anymore |[var1 |[flurry.name] is not pregnant |You are not pregnant ] ], but you also don’t have a kip added to your clutch; instead, you have an egg the size of a human baby, with a smooth white shell, sitting listlessly either on the ice or underneath [flurry.name] as he nests on it. Though the egg is apart from [var1 |[flurry.name] |you ], you still have a psionic connection with the kip incubating inside it: occasionally, sensations are broadcast to you from the kip inside, but they don’t feel like communications – at least, not the same way that you and [flurry.name] communicate. They feel more primeval, and practically accidental: what you feel are raw emotions with no forethought or justification to them. Sometimes, the kip is fussy and uncomfortable, and that makes you uncomfortable; sometimes, especially if either you or [flurry.name] stray too far, it gets anxious; sometimes, you get the urge to wear a big, goofy smile on your face for minutes at a time, just because the kip feels that way, too. After the first month of incubation, the egg has become visibly larger, the shell stretching to accommodate the kip inside of it. It’s almost as if the shell itself had scales and was a part of the kip’s body rather than a protective covering that the kip is meant to break out of once it’s ready. The kip inside of it is getting much, much larger: the egg shifts and jostles with the kip’s movements inside of it, and when you put your hand to the shell’s surface, sometimes, you think you can feel the kip’s hand press back against you. By the end of the second month of incubation, the kip inside the egg was forming proper words with its psionics. Or... rather, it was forming proper thoughts to express those words. You would ‘feel’ that it’s thinking of the word ‘Qal,’ and you’d know that it was thinking of you. It’d think of the word ‘warm,’ and you’d know that it’d be asking for its Qim and Qal to cuddle against it for warmth. By the end of the third month, it was managing to put more than one thought together to form something akin to a sentence. All the while, the egg itself kept growing at a surprising rate, until [pc.heightRange 0 84 96 |it was significantly taller than you are |it became a little bit taller than you are |it nearly got as tall as you are ]. At the end of the fourth month, while you and [flurry.name] were speaking with [frostwyrm.name] on the quality of their recent catch of fish, you hear the distinct, sharp sound of an eggshell cracking apart. You and [flurry.name] rush to the egg to find that its rounded top had been pierced by what appeared to be a wingtip; with another concerted thrust from its body, the kip kicks its arms and legs, and the cracks in the shell draw much deeper along its oblong length, but not enough for the egg to split apart. [flurry.name] thinks to maybe try and help the kip out by breaking the shell in pieces, but you stop him: it’s important for the kip’s development that it does its very first task as a living creature by itself. It takes some time, but, eventually, the kip manages to break free by puncturing several small holes in the egg’s shell with its pointed claws and horns. After several tense minutes, your draconic kip lies on the lair’s icy floor, covered in bits of egg shell. [var0 |[var2 |For the first time since you and [frostwyrm.name] became a family, the kip that hatches from the egg isn’t a halfling – it’s a real, pureblood Frostwyrm, with [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name]’s genes coursing through them. It’s worked: your efforts to help conserve and rescue the Frostwyrms of Uveto are paying off, and you have the real, tangible, breathing results to prove it. |As you had expected from your conservation efforts, the kip that hatches from the egg is a pureblood Frostwyrm: a kip that doesn’t bear any sort of resemblance to you at all. It’s a true, pureblood Frostwyrm, with the same physiology as [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] – but, inextricably, with you as its Qal. Once more, your efforts to save the Frostwyrms are paying off. ] Despite its size, it doesn’t have the same ferocious, implacable, imposing countenance as either of its Qims: where [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] are covered in a thick, scaly hide, the new kip’s skin is so thin as to almost be translucent. Its tail has no spikes and is smooth from pelvis to tip. It has teeth, but they’re small and nubby and wouldn’t pierce a slice of bread, if it even had the jaw strength. It has four eyes, but all of them are shut tight. As is usual for your newborns, it’s blind, cold, exhausted, and its psionic link with you and its Qims is weak, but you can tell that it’s calling out to you. You get into your usual position with [frostwyrm.name] – but both she and [flurry.name] are the Qim to this one, and there they initially struggle with their instincts in getting into a proper position to coddle their newborn kip. It takes a bit of effort, but they figure it out. |Unsurprisingly, your kip with [flurry.name] doesn’t look much different from your kips with [frostwyrm.name]. Seven feet tall; two legs; four arms; a massive wingspan. It’s hard to believe something so massive is so young, but then again, it has its draconic Qim to compare itself to. Despite its size, it’s blind, cold, and exhausted; its psionic link with you is weak, though you can tell that it’s calling out for you and [flurry.name]. And, being the good parents that you are, you’re quick to place your kip between your bodies for warmth, with [flurry.name] draping his wing across you for added shelter. ] It’ll be a while yet before your kip is ready to join the rest of your clutch, never mind the world at large, but that’s not something you need to worry about right now. Right now, what’s important is that you have another addition to your family. That said, though: from your experiences with [frostwyrm.name] and child-rearing with her, you know that it’ll be another four months until its fully mature, enough to the point that it’ll be able to live on its own if needed. Your duty as the Qal is to ensure that your kip grows with the tools and knowledge necessary to live a comfortable life. It’d be wrong of you to leave your family now when they need you the most. The hardest part of raising a Frostwyrm is over: now, it’s time you fulfill your duties as Qal.
rows.translation: 蛋或许已经产下，但它还没有孵化，在它破壳之前，你还不能理直气壮地说自己的窝里又添了一只幼崽。尽管没有你在场时它并不会孵化，你仍无论如何都不愿错过其中的任何一刻。 说实话，孵蛋的第一个月相当无聊。[var3 |你和[flurry.name]都已不再怀孕 |[var1 |[flurry.name]并未怀孕 |你并未怀孕 ] ]，但你的窝里同样还没有增添幼崽；取而代之的是一枚人类婴儿大小、外壳光滑洁白的蛋，它无精打采地待在冰面上，或是待在筑巢孵蛋的[flurry.name]身下。 尽管这枚蛋与[var1 |[flurry.name] |你 ]彼此分离，你与其中正在孵化的幼崽仍有心灵感应连接：偶尔，里面的幼崽会把感觉传递给你，但那并不像是交流，至少不像你和[flurry.name]之间的交流。它们更为原始，几乎完全出于无意；你感受到的是未经思考、也不需要理由的纯粹情绪。有时幼崽焦躁不安，连带着让你也感到不适；有时，尤其是你或[flurry.name]离得太远时，它会变得焦虑；还有时，你会莫名想在脸上挂着傻乎乎的灿烂笑容，一笑就是好几分钟，只因为幼崽也正有同样的感受。 孵化一个月后，蛋已经明显变大，蛋壳随之延展，以容纳里面的幼崽。那蛋壳仿佛自身也长着鳞片，是幼崽身体的一部分，而非等幼崽准备好后便要破壳而出的保护层。里面的幼崽正变得越来越大：蛋会随着幼崽在其中活动而摇晃、挪动；当你把手贴在蛋壳表面时，有时甚至觉得能感到幼崽将手掌贴回来。 到了孵化的第二个月末，蛋里的幼崽已经开始用心灵感应组织出正确的词语。或者说...它开始形成能够表达那些词语的完整思绪。你会“感觉”到它正在想着“Qal”这个词，也会明白它想的是你。它会想到“温暖”这个词，而你则会明白，它是在请求自己的Qim和Qal贴着它依偎，为它取暖。到了第三个月末，它已能把不止一个念头组合起来，形成近似句子的表达。在此期间，蛋本身始终以惊人的速度生长，直到[pc.heightRange 0 84 96 |它变得比你高出许多 |它变得比你稍高一些 |它几乎长到了与你一样高 ]。 第四个月末，当你和[flurry.name]正与[frostwyrm.name]谈论他们最近捕获的鱼品质如何时，你听见了蛋壳破裂时清脆而鲜明的声音。你和[flurry.name]冲到蛋旁，发现它圆润的顶部已被似乎是翼尖的东西刺穿；幼崽再次调动全身奋力一顶，同时挥蹬四肢，裂纹便沿着椭圆形蛋壳向更深处延伸，但还不足以让整枚蛋裂开。[flurry.name]想着也许可以敲碎蛋壳，帮助幼崽出来，但你阻止了他：作为一个活着的生物，独自完成生命中的第一项任务，对幼崽的成长十分重要。 这花了一些时间，但幼崽最终还是用尖锐的爪子和犄角在蛋壳上凿出数个小洞，成功挣脱出来。紧张的几分钟过后，你的龙族幼崽躺在巢穴的冰冷地面上，浑身沾满蛋壳碎片。 [var0 |[var2 |自从你和[frostwyrm.name]成为一家人以来，这是第一次，从蛋中孵出的幼崽并非混血儿，而是一条真正的纯血霜龙，体内流淌着[frostwyrm.name]与[flurry.name]的血脉。成功了：你为保护和拯救乌维托霜龙所做的努力正在取得成果，而眼前这真实、可触、正在呼吸的生命就是证明。 |正如你对保育工作所预期的那样，从蛋中孵出的幼崽是一条纯血霜龙，一只完全没有任何地方与你相似的幼崽。它是货真价实的纯血霜龙，拥有与[frostwyrm.name]和[flurry.name]相同的身体构造，却又与你有着无法割舍的联系，认你为它的Qal。你拯救霜龙的努力又一次取得了成果。 ] 尽管体型庞大，它却没有两位Qim那般凶猛、冷酷而威严的面容：[frostwyrm.name]和[flurry.name]都覆盖着厚实的鳞皮，这只新生幼崽的皮肤却薄得几乎透明。它的尾巴没有尖刺，从骨盆到尾尖都十分光滑。它长着牙齿，但牙齿又小又钝，哪怕它有足够的咬合力，也刺不穿一片面包。它有四只眼睛，但全都紧紧闭着。 和你其他的新生儿一样，它双目失明、身体冰冷、筋疲力尽，与你及其Qim之间的心灵感应也很微弱，但你能察觉到它正在呼唤你。你与[frostwyrm.name]摆出平时的姿势，但这一次她和[flurry.name]都是幼崽的Qim，起初两人还在本能驱使下手忙脚乱，不知该怎样摆好姿势呵护新生的幼崽。他们费了一番工夫，不过最终还是弄明白了。 |不出所料，你和[flurry.name]的幼崽看起来与[frostwyrm.name]为你生下的那些幼崽相差无几。七英尺高，两条腿，四条手臂，还有一对翼展宽阔的巨翼。如此庞大的生物竟然如此年幼，实在难以置信，但话说回来，它有一位龙族Qim可以作为参照。 尽管体型庞大，它却双目失明、身体冰冷而且筋疲力尽；它与你之间的心灵感应很微弱，但你能察觉到它正在呼唤你和[flurry.name]。作为称职的双亲，你们很快便把幼崽放在彼此的身体之间取暖，[flurry.name]还将翅膀覆在你们身上，提供额外的庇护。 ] 你的幼崽还要过上一段时间才能加入窝里的其他成员，更别说走向外面的广阔世界了，不过你现在无需为此担忧。此刻最重要的是，你的家庭又增添了一名新成员。 不过，从你与[frostwyrm.name]共同养育孩子的经历来看，你知道还要再过四个月，它才会完全成熟，成长到必要时能够独立生活的程度。身为Qal，你有责任确保幼崽在成长过程中掌握过上舒适生活所必需的工具与知识。 家人最需要你的时候，抛下他们离去是不对的。养育霜龙最艰难的阶段已经结束，现在，该由你履行身为Qal的职责了。
rows.raw: " The egg may be laid, but it’s not yet hatched – you can’t rightly say you’ve added another kip to your clutch until it has. While it’s not about to hatch without you here, you’re still not going to miss any bit of it for the world. The first month of the egg incubation was admittedly rather boring. [var3 |Neither you nor [flurry.name] are pregnant anymore |[var1 |[flurry.name] is not pregnant |You are not pregnant ] ], but you also don’t have a kip added to your clutch; instead, you have an egg the size of a human baby, with a smooth white shell, sitting listlessly either on the ice or underneath [flurry.name] as he nests on it. Though the egg is apart from [var1 |[flurry.name] |you ], you still have a psionic connection with the kip incubating inside it: occasionally, sensations are broadcast to you from the kip inside, but they don’t feel like communications – at least, not the same way that you and [flurry.name] communicate. They feel more primeval, and practically accidental: what you feel are raw emotions with no forethought or justification to them. Sometimes, the kip is fussy and uncomfortable, and that makes you uncomfortable; sometimes, especially if either you or [flurry.name] stray too far, it gets anxious; sometimes, you get the urge to wear a big, goofy smile on your face for minutes at a time, just because the kip feels that way, too. After the first month of incubation, the egg has become visibly larger, the shell stretching to accommodate the kip inside of it. It’s almost as if the shell itself had scales and was a part of the kip’s body rather than a protective covering that the kip is meant to break out of once it’s ready. The kip inside of it is getting much, much larger: the egg shifts and jostles with the kip’s movements inside of it, and when you put your hand to the shell’s surface, sometimes, you think you can feel the kip’s hand press back against you. By the end of the second month of incubation, the kip inside the egg was forming proper words with its psionics. Or... rather, it was forming proper thoughts to express those words. You would ‘feel’ that it’s thinking of the word ‘Qal,’ and you’d know that it was thinking of you. It’d think of the word ‘warm,’ and you’d know that it’d be asking for its Qim and Qal to cuddle against it for warmth. By the end of the third month, it was managing to put more than one thought together to form something akin to a sentence. All the while, the egg itself kept growing at a surprising rate, until [pc.heightRange 0 84 96 |it was significantly taller than you are |it became a little bit taller than you are |it nearly got as tall as you are ]. At the end of the fourth month, while you and [flurry.name] were speaking with [frostwyrm.name] on the quality of their recent catch of fish, you hear the distinct, sharp sound of an eggshell cracking apart. You and [flurry.name] rush to the egg to find that its rounded top had been pierced by what appeared to be a wingtip; with another concerted thrust from its body, the kip kicks its arms and legs, and the cracks in the shell draw much deeper along its oblong length, but not enough for the egg to split apart. [flurry.name] thinks to maybe try and help the kip out by breaking the shell in pieces, but you stop him: it’s important for the kip’s development that it does its very first task as a living creature by itself. It takes some time, but, eventually, the kip manages to break free by puncturing several small holes in the egg’s shell with its pointed claws and horns. After several tense minutes, your draconic kip lies on the lair’s icy floor, covered in bits of egg shell. [var0 |[var2 |For the first time since you and [frostwyrm.name] became a family, the kip that hatches from the egg isn’t a halfling – it’s a real, pureblood Frostwyrm, with [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name]’s genes coursing through them. It’s worked: your efforts to help conserve and rescue the Frostwyrms of Uveto are paying off, and you have the real, tangible, breathing results to prove it. |As you had expected from your conservation efforts, the kip that hatches from the egg is a pureblood Frostwyrm: a kip that doesn’t bear any sort of resemblance to you at all. It’s a true, pureblood Frostwyrm, with the same physiology as [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] – but, inextricably, with you as its Qal. Once more, your efforts to save the Frostwyrms are paying off. ] Despite its size, it doesn’t have the same ferocious, implacable, imposing countenance as either of its Qims: where [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] are covered in a thick, scaly hide, the new kip’s skin is so thin as to almost be translucent. Its tail has no spikes and is smooth from pelvis to tip. It has teeth, but they’re small and nubby and wouldn’t pierce a slice of bread, if it even had the jaw strength. It has four eyes, but all of them are shut tight. As is usual for your newborns, it’s blind, cold, exhausted, and its psionic link with you and its Qims is weak, but you can tell that it’s calling out to you. You get into your usual position with [frostwyrm.name] – but both she and [flurry.name] are the Qim to this one, and there they initially struggle with their instincts in getting into a proper position to coddle their newborn kip. It takes a bit of effort, but they figure it out. |Unsurprisingly, your kip with [flurry.name] doesn’t look much different from your kips with [frostwyrm.name]. Seven feet tall; two legs; four arms; a massive wingspan. It’s hard to believe something so massive is so young, but then again, it has its draconic Qim to compare itself to. Despite its size, it’s blind, cold, and exhausted; its psionic link with you is weak, though you can tell that it’s calling out for you and [flurry.name]. And, being the good parents that you are, you’re quick to place your kip between your bodies for warmth, with [flurry.name] draping his wing across you for added shelter. ] It’ll be a while yet before your kip is ready to join the rest of your clutch, never mind the world at large, but that’s not something you need to worry about right now. The hardest part of raising a Frostwyrm is over: now, it’s time you fulfill your duties as Qal. "

rows.original: 4 Months...
rows.translation: 四个月...
rows.raw: "4 Months..."

rows.original: It’ll be another four months before your kip will be mature enough that, by Frostwyrm standards, it should be able to live, hunt, and survive on its own, without the aid of its Qim or Qal. Although kips don’t leave the nest until their parents pass away, they’re still expected to do their part around the home in some form or another, be it hunting, or defending the nest against poachers, or whatever the clutch needs most at the time. The first month is spent teaching the kip how to communicate in ways that you can easily interpret. [flurry.name] can understand everything your kip wants just from feeling the emotions that the kip has at any given time – and [frostwyrm.name] often said that she preferred to communicate via emotions than with words – but it’s a minor hurdle for you to get over as the Qal. Frostwyrms are intelligent dragons, and by the end of the month, your kip was communicating with you in full sentences. [var0 |The next two months were teaching the kip how to survive out in the Uveto wilderness. While the kip is a pureblood, hexapedal dragon and not a biped like the rest of your kips, it’s still up to you, the Qal, to teach it how to hunt and survive. Fortunately, it’s not so difficult: you’ve gotten used to the colds of the planet, and teaching the kip to remain camouflaged in the snow as it preys on its targets isn’t a difficult thing to pass on. You teach it to always aim for the neck; to never face away from its prey or any attackers; and to never take on something larger than it, if it can. It turns out that living with [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] for so long has taught you a few things about how to act like a Frostwyrm, as well. |The next two months were teaching the kip how to fashion tools and how to survive with its bipedal body. Normally, [flurry.name] would have been the one to teach the kip how to hunt, but your kip is bipedal; it’s you that teaches it how to use nets and spears and how best to camouflage itself in the white snow of Uveto[pc.intelligenceRange 0 30 |. Although, and you keep this to yourself, it’s all a learning experience to you, too – thank heavens for the extranet! |. ][frostwyrm.andNykke | Thankfully, Nykke is there to help you explain things to your kip in ways that it could more easily understand; you might be the Qal, but Nykke is a Frostwyrmling herself, and she knows better the struggles that a developing kip might have with ‘asymmetrical’ parents like you and [flurry.name]. ] ] The fourth and final month isn’t spent on learning to hunt or teaching it how to fend for itself – it’s already picked up everything you could teach it. The last month is spent in equal parts [var0 |[frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] |[flurry.name][frostwyrm.andNykke | and Nykke ] ] teaching your kip how to fly, and you teaching your kip the concept of ethics and morality. Frostwyrms are a noble species, and while [pc.race]s aren’t exactly paragons themselves, your whole relationship with [var0 |both of your Qims started on[flags.FLURRY_VICTORY | especially ] rocky terms |[flurry.name] started on[flags.FLURRY_VICTORY | especially ] rocky terms ]; it’s an unfortunate fact that Frostwyrms are an endangered species and that Frostwyrm[var0 | |lings ] like your kip might be the last chance they have from extinction. It’s important that it understands how to treat others with respect, since everyone’s in the same boat – and when to recognize that it’s not being returned. At the end of the fourth month, your kip is fully matured: it stands roughly [var0 |eighteen feet tall, with still a bit of room left to grow |ten feet tall ]; it knows how to fly, hunt, and empathize; and it’s ready to start contributing to the clutch. Watching it leave the lair to hunt for food to bring back is exciting, but, in a way, bittersweet[var0 |. It’s a good thing the lair is as gigantic and vacant as it is, if you’re going to be Qal to many more purebloods, if they’re all going to grow to be that size! |. ] [var0 |And that’s... that. You’ve done it: you’ve raised a pureblood kip with [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] from conceptualization to maturity, and now it’s a pure, real, healthy Frostwyrm. One more to add to a world that was once filled with majestic frost dragons before they had started to die out. You look to [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name]. This could work. You could rescue the Frostwyrms, with a bit more effort... and a little bit of luck. If there are others out there, then surely your kips will find them. But just adding one more Frostwyrm to the pool isn’t going to increase the odds all that much. You know that; [frostwyrm.name] knows that; and [flurry.name] knows that. You’ll just have to make another one, and soon. |You rest against [flurry.name]’s stomach; the feeling of contentment you both have is all-encompassing. You’ve both done your duties as Qim and Qal. You look up at [flurry.name]’s face just as he looks down at yours. You both have the same thought at the same time. You’re both in the mood to do it all over again. Starting with your next kip’s conceptualization.... ]
rows.translation: 还要再过四个月，你的幼崽才会成熟到以霜龙的标准而言，能够不依靠Qim或Qal，独自生活、狩猎并生存下去的程度。尽管幼崽直到父母去世才会离巢，它们仍被期望以某种方式为家中尽一份力，无论是狩猎、抵御偷猎者保卫巢穴，还是完成窝里当时最需要它们做的任何事情。 第一个月用于教导幼崽如何以你容易理解的方式交流。[flurry.name]仅凭感受幼崽当下的情绪，便能理解它想要的一切，而[frostwyrm.name]也经常说，与词语相比，她更喜欢通过情绪交流，但对身为Qal的你而言，这只是一道需要克服的小障碍。霜龙是聪慧的龙族，到这个月结束时，你的幼崽已经能用完整的句子与你交流。 [var0 |接下来的两个月用于教导幼崽如何在乌维托的荒野中生存。尽管它是一条纯血的六足龙，不像你的其他幼崽那样用双足行走，教它如何狩猎和求生依然是你这位Qal的责任。幸运的是，这并不太困难：你已经适应了这颗星球的严寒，教幼崽在捕猎目标时如何藏身于积雪之中，也不是什么难以传授的技巧。你教它始终瞄准脖颈，绝不能背对猎物或任何袭击者，并且只要能够避免，就绝不挑战体型比它更大的东西。事实证明，与[frostwyrm.name]和[flurry.name]生活了这么久，也让你学会了一些如何像霜龙一样行动的诀窍。 |接下来的两个月用于教导幼崽如何制作工具，以及如何凭借双足直立的身体生存。通常本该由[flurry.name]教幼崽狩猎，但你的幼崽是双足直立的；于是由你教它如何使用网和长矛，以及怎样才能最好地藏身于乌维托的白雪之中[pc.intelligenceRange 0 30 |。不过，这一点你没有说出口，对你而言，这一切同样也是学习的过程，感谢天外网络！ |。 ][frostwyrm.andNykke | 值得庆幸的是，妮凯也在场，可以用幼崽更容易理解的方式帮你向它解释；你或许是Qal，但妮凯自己也是一只霜龙幼体，她比你更了解发育中的幼崽面对你和[flurry.name]这样“不对称”的双亲时可能遇到的困难。 ] ] 第四个也是最后一个月并不用来学习狩猎或教它如何自卫，因为它已经掌握了你能教给它的一切。最后一个月由[var0 |[frostwyrm.name]和[flurry.name] |[flurry.name][frostwyrm.andNykke |与妮凯 ] ]教导幼崽飞行，而你则教导幼崽伦理与道德观念，双方各占一半时间。霜龙是高贵的种族，虽然[pc.race]也称不上什么道德典范，但你与[var0 |两位Qim的整段关系始于[flags.FLURRY_VICTORY |格外 ]坎坷的局面 |[flurry.name]的整段关系始于[flags.FLURRY_VICTORY |格外 ]坎坷的局面 ]；遗憾的是，霜龙已是濒危物种，而像你的幼崽这样尚且年幼的霜龙[var0 | |幼体 ]，或许正是它们免于灭绝的最后希望。它必须明白该如何尊重他人，因为大家都身处同一条船上，同时也要学会辨认自己的尊重何时没有得到回报。 第四个月结束时，你的幼崽已经完全成熟：它大约有[var0 |十八英尺高，而且还留有少许生长空间 |十英尺高 ]；它学会了飞行、狩猎和体谅他人，也已经准备好开始为窝里作出贡献。看着它离开巢穴外出捕猎，为家里带回食物，令人兴奋，却也在某种意义上令人感伤[var0 |。如果你还要成为更多纯血幼崽的Qal，而且它们个个都会长到这般体型，那么幸好这座巢穴足够巨大而且空旷！ |。 ] [var0 |就这样...结束了。你成功了：你和[frostwyrm.name]、[flurry.name]一起，将一只纯血幼崽从孕育之初抚养至成熟，而现在它已经是一条纯正、真实而健康的霜龙。在这个曾经遍布雄伟冰霜巨龙、后来却目睹它们逐渐凋零的世界上，又多了一名族群成员。 你望向[frostwyrm.name]和[flurry.name]。这办法行得通。再多付出一点努力...再加上一点运气，你们就能拯救霜龙。如果世上还有其他霜龙，那么你的幼崽们一定会找到它们。 但仅仅再为族群增添一条霜龙，并不会大幅提高成功的概率。你知道这一点，[frostwyrm.name]知道，[flurry.name]也知道。 你们只能再造一只，而且要尽快。 |你靠在[flurry.name]的腹部；你们共同感受到的满足感充盈全身。你们都已履行了作为Qim和Qal的职责。 你抬头望向[flurry.name]的脸庞，恰好他也低头看向你。你们同时产生了相同的念头。 你们都兴致勃勃，想把这一切再来一遍。 就从孕育下一只幼崽开始.... ]
rows.raw: " It’ll be another four months before your kip will be mature enough that, by Frostwyrm standards, it should be able to live, hunt, and survive on its own, without the aid of its Qim or Qal. Although kips don’t leave the nest until their parents pass away, they’re still expected to do their part around the home in some form or another, be it hunting, or defending the nest against poachers, or whatever the clutch needs most at the time. The first month is spent teaching the kip how to communicate in ways that you can easily interpret. [flurry.name] can understand everything your kip wants just from feeling the emotions that the kip has at any given time – and [frostwyrm.name] often said that she preferred to communicate via emotions than with words – but it’s a minor hurdle for you to get over as the Qal. Frostwyrms are intelligent dragons, and by the end of the month, your kip was communicating with you in full sentences. [var0 |The next two months were teaching the kip how to survive out in the Uveto wilderness. While the kip is a pureblood, hexapedal dragon and not a biped like the rest of your kips, it’s still up to you, the Qal, to teach it how to hunt and survive. Fortunately, it’s not so difficult: you’ve gotten used to the colds of the planet, and teaching the kip to remain camouflaged in the snow as it preys on its targets isn’t a difficult thing to pass on. You teach it to always aim for the neck; to never face away from its prey or any attackers; and to never take on something larger than it, if it can. It turns out that living with [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] for so long has taught you a few things about how to act like a Frostwyrm, as well. |The next two months were teaching the kip how to fashion tools and how to survive with its bipedal body. Normally, [flurry.name] would have been the one to teach the kip how to hunt, but your kip is bipedal; it’s you that teaches it how to use nets and spears and how best to camouflage itself in the white snow of Uveto[pc.intelligenceRange 0 30 |. Although, and you keep this to yourself, it’s all a learning experience to you, too – thank heavens for the extranet! |. ][frostwyrm.andNykke | Thankfully, Nykke is there to help you explain things to your kip in ways that it could more easily understand; you might be the Qal, but Nykke is a Frostwyrmling herself, and she knows better the struggles that a developing kip might have with ‘asymmetrical’ parents like you and [flurry.name]. ] ] The fourth and final month isn’t spent on learning to hunt or teaching it how to fend for itself – it’s already picked up everything you could teach it. The last month is spent in equal parts [var0 |[frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] |[flurry.name][frostwyrm.andNykke | and Nykke ] ] teaching your kip how to fly, and you teaching your kip the concept of ethics and morality. Frostwyrms are a noble species, and while [pc.race]s aren’t exactly paragons themselves, your whole relationship with [var0 |both of your Qims started on[flags.FLURRY_VICTORY | especially ] rocky terms |[flurry.name] started on[flags.FLURRY_VICTORY | especially ] rocky terms ]; it’s an unfortunate fact that Frostwyrms are an endangered species and that Frostwyrm[var0 | |lings ] like your kip might be the last chance they have from extinction. It’s important that it understands how to treat others with respect, since everyone’s in the same boat – and when to recognize that it’s not being returned. At the end of the fourth month, your kip is fully matured: it stands roughly [var0 |eighteen feet tall, with still a bit of room left to grow |ten feet tall ]; it knows how to fly, hunt, and empathize; and it’s ready to start contributing to the clutch. Watching it leave the lair to hunt for food to bring back is exciting, but, in a way, bittersweet[var0 |. It’s a good thing the lair is as gigantic and vacant as it is, if you’re going to be Qal to many more purebloods, if they’re all going to grow to be that size! |. ] [var0 |And that’s... that. You’ve done it: you’ve raised a pureblood kip with [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name] from conceptualization to maturity, and now it’s a pure, real, healthy Frostwyrm. One more to add to a world that was once filled with majestic frost dragons before they had started to die out. You look to [frostwyrm.name] and [flurry.name]. This could work. You could rescue the Frostwyrms, with a bit more effort... and a little bit of luck. If there are others out there, then surely your kips will find them. But just adding one more Frostwyrm to the pool isn’t going to increase the odds all that much. You know that; [frostwyrm.name] knows that; and [flurry.name] knows that. You’ll just have to make another one, and soon. |You rest against [flurry.name]’s stomach; the feeling of contentment you both have is all-encompassing. You’ve both done your duties as Qim and Qal. You look up at [flurry.name]’s face just as he looks down at yours. You both have the same thought at the same time. You’re both in the mood to do it all over again. Starting with your next kip’s conceptualization.... ] "

rows.translation: 你仍有事情要做，也有地方要去 – 但当初同意成为不只一条[frostwyrm.andNykke|、也不只两条，而是三条|、而是两条]龙的Qal时，你就知道自己会面对什么。毕竟，霜龙正处在灭绝边缘；他们需要你留在乌维托时，你却在宇宙中四处游荡，实在是不负责任。 [flurry.name]从鼻间发出一声沉重而悠长的叹息，放松地趴在你身上，脑袋也越来越沉地压在你的腿上。即使你们之间没有灵能连接，你也能看出这个消息令他如释重负。他真的很期待成为一名称职的Qim，照顾好你。 你给飞船发去消息，表示自己将有一段时间无法脱身，但没有说明详情。之后，你要做的就只是放松下来，等待这枚蛋从体内出来....
rows.raw: " There are still things that you need to do and places that you need to be – but you knew what you were getting into when you agreed to be the Qal to not just one[frostwyrm.andNykke|, and not just two, but three|, but two] dragons. Frostwyrms are on the brink of extinction, after all; it would be irresponsible of you to go gallivanting around the cosmos when they need you here on Uveto. [flurry.name] heaves a long, heavy sigh through his nose, and you feel his head getting heavier on your lap as he relaxes on top of you. Even if you didn’t have your psionic link with him, you can tell that this news is a huge relief. He’s really looking forward to being a good Qim for you. You send a message to your ship that you’re going to be indisposed for a time, but you don’t give specifics. After that, it’s just a matter of kicking back and waiting for this egg to pop out of you.... "

rows.original: If there’s any one thing you’ve learned during your time with [frostwyrm.name] so far, it’s that Frostwyrm eggs are pretty hardy. A bit of adventuring isn’t going to be a threat to your kip while it’s inside you. Are you certain? [flurry.name] asks, his eyes lifting up to meet yours. There’s an undeniable feeling of anxiety coursing through your psionic link with him as the words enter your mind. I.... You patiently wait for him to continue. I was looking forward to being a Qim, he admits. You aren’t robbing him of that opportunity out of malice or anything; you, as a [pc.race], have other responsibilities that you must tend to. Being a Qal is a full-time job! You promise that you’ll come straight back to the lair whenever you get a moment’s peace. He takes a long, somewhat-dejected sigh through his nose. I understand, he says, and although you’re sure he does, you can tell that he can’t help but feel disappointed in your decision.
rows.translation: 截至目前，和[frostwyrm.name]相处期间你若学到了什么，那就是霜龙蛋相当坚韧。趁幼崽还在你体内时稍微冒险一番，并不会威胁到它。 你确定吗？[flurry.name]问道，抬眼望向你。话语进入脑海时，一股毋庸置疑的焦虑正沿着你们之间的灵能连接奔涌而来。我.... 你耐心等他继续说下去。 我一直很期待成为Qim，他坦白道。 你并不是出于恶意要夺走他的这个机会；身为[pc.race]，你还有其他必须履行的责任。担任Qal可是份全职工作！你向他保证，只要一有片刻安闲，就会直接回到巢穴。 他从鼻间发出一声悠长而略显沮丧的叹息。我明白，他说道。你确信他的确明白，但也看得出来，他仍忍不住对你的决定感到失望。

A bit of adventuring isn’t going to be a threat to your kip while it’s inside you. Are you certain? [flurry.name] asks, his eyes lifting up to meet yours. There’s an undeniable feeling of anxiety coursing through your psionic link with him as the words enter your mind. I.... You patiently wait for him to continue. I was looking forward to being a Qim, he admits. You aren’t robbing him of that opportunity out of malice or anything; you, as a [pc.race], have other responsibilities that you must tend to. Being a Qal is a full-time job! You promise that you’ll come straight back to the lair whenever you get a moment’s peace. He takes a long, somewhat-dejected sigh through his nose. I understand, he says, and although you’re sure he does, you can tell that he can’t help but feel disappointed in your decision. "

rows.original: On the one hand, you’re the Qal to [frostwyrm.andNykke |three |two ] very devoted dragons: you so much as say a word and [frostwyrm.andNykke |any |both ] of them are at your total beck and call, willing to give you whatever it is you need. Whether it’s food; warmth; sex; or just some companionship; you have everything you could need while [flurry.name] leaps at every opportunity to provide for you, as a proper Qim ought to. On the other, though: not only does that mean the next four months of your life will lack any sort of challenge, it also makes things routine and boring. You’re barely allowed to leave the lair – you’re given supervised visits to the island’s surface whenever you want, but they won’t take you past the shoreline – and although they’re willing to sate your urges whenever you need, they won’t do anything more imaginative or physically demanding like you know a pair of dragons with cocks the size of adult [pc.race] bodies are capable of. And, to be honest, you’re kind of sick of the taste of fish. You’re the Qal: if you really put your foot down and made some demands, you know they’d acquiesce. If you really, really wanted to leave, they wouldn’t stop you. They do what they do because they care about you and your kip. But that really only makes your cage just a little more gilded, as it were. By the end of the second month, you had begun showing: your stomach rounded out and your body began to go through some obvious changes, particularly to your gait as you go from walking across the lair to waddling. Life isn’t any more difficult, largely in part because [frostwyrm.andNykke |your dragons |[flurry.name] and [frostwyrm.name] ] won’t let it be, but it does get a little more awkward. Life progresses fairly slowly: the next two more months are more of the same, with your body changing a bit more with each passing day and your stomach getting rounder and rounder. Although, your stomach does feel a little tight as the egg gets larger: something you attribute to the fact that Frostwyrm gestation is typically much faster than [pc.race] gestation. The kip developing inside of you is capable of some rudimentary psionics: it can broadcast emotions and does so at random times with random intensities, often without any warning or forethought to them; it’s almost as if the kip isn’t aware that it exists and is broadcasting emotions to you and [flurry.name] in spite of that. By the end of the fourth month, it’s getting harder to walk and the weight makes getting up or lying down a bit of a chore. Sleeping against [flurry.name] helps alleviate the stress a little bit, and his psionics help block whatever discomforts you have, but the reality is that you have a baby-sized egg inside of you that’s ready to come out any day now. Eventually, that day arrives: with an awkward jerk inside of your womb, you feel the instinctive need to lay the egg and get it out of you. Thankfully, the egg isn’t any larger than a typical [pc.race] baby, and its smooth shell and shape make it easier than you had expected to pass – but none of that is to suggest that it’s easy. It’s an arduous process that’s made slightly easier by [flurry.name] blocking your pain psionically. By the end of the ordeal, you’re left with an oblong Frostwyrm egg – and a bit of baby fat that you need to burn off. Frostwyrm gestation involves both of the parents being present for the egg’s development cycle: without both its Qim and Qal present, the egg will simply not hatch unless both you and [flurry.name] are there to incubate it. Hatching the egg will take another four months. It’s not like the egg will be going anywhere until it’s ready, but you could spend some more quality time with your [frostwyrm.andNykke |three |two ] Qims....
rows.translation: 一方面，你是[frostwyrm.andNykke |三条 |两条 ]极其忠诚的龙的Qal：只要你说上一句话，[frostwyrm.andNykke |他们中的任何一条 |他们两个 ]便会完全听从你的吩咐，愿意满足你的一切需要。无论是食物、温暖、性爱，还是单纯的陪伴；你所需的一切应有尽有，而[flurry.name]会抓住每一个机会照顾你，正如一名合格的Qim理应做到的那样。 但另一方面：这不仅意味着你接下来四个月的人生不会有任何挑战，也让生活变得一成不变、枯燥乏味。你几乎不获准离开巢穴 – 你想去岛屿地表时，可以在他们陪同下外出，但他们不会带你越过海岸线 – 而且尽管他们愿意随时满足你的欲望，却不会做任何更有创意或对体力要求更高的事情，明明你知道两条肉棒大如成年[pc.race]身体的龙完全做得到。老实说，你也有点吃腻鱼了。 你是Qal：如果你真的摆出强硬态度、提出要求，你知道他们会顺从。假如你真的、真的想离开，他们也不会阻止你。他们这么做，是因为关心你和你的幼崽。不过话说回来，这也只是让你的牢笼镀上了一层薄薄的金罢了。 到第二个月结束时，你已经显怀了：腹部逐渐隆起，身体也开始出现一些明显变化，尤其是步态，你从在巢穴里走动变成了摇摇摆摆地挪动。生活并没有变得更困难，很大程度上是因为[frostwyrm.andNykke |你的龙们 |[flurry.name]和[frostwyrm.name] ]绝不会允许这种事发生，但确实变得有些笨拙不便。 日子过得相当缓慢：接下来的两个月仍是同样的生活，你的身体一天天继续变化，腹部也越来越圆。不过随着蛋逐渐长大，你的肚子确实感觉有些紧绷：你将其归因于霜龙的妊娠期通常比[pc.race]短得多。体内正在发育的幼崽已经具备一些初步灵能：它会广播情绪，时间和强度都毫无规律，而且常常毫无预兆，也完全不经思考；仿佛幼崽甚至还没意识到自己的存在，却依然把情绪传递给你和[flurry.name]。 到第四个月结束时，走路已越发困难，沉重的分量让起身或躺下都成了件麻烦事。靠着[flurry.name]睡觉能稍微缓解压力，他的灵能也有助于隔绝你的不适，但现实是，你体内有一枚婴儿大小、随时都会产出的蛋。 终于，那一天到来了：子宫里突兀地一动，你本能地感到需要把蛋产出体外。幸好这枚蛋并不比普通的[pc.race]婴儿更大，光滑的蛋壳与外形也让它比预想中更容易通过产道 – 但这绝不意味着过程轻松。整个生产过程艰苦异常，只因[flurry.name]用灵能隔绝你的疼痛，才略微好受一些。 折腾结束后，你身边多了一枚椭圆形的霜龙蛋 – 还有一点需要减掉的产后赘肉。 霜龙的孕育过程要求双亲共同参与蛋的发育周期：如果Qim和Qal不同时在场，蛋就不会孵化，除非你和[flurry.name]都在这里为它孵育。 蛋还要四个月才能孵化。反正它在准备好之前也不会跑掉，不过你可以和自己的[frostwyrm.andNykke |三名 |两名 ]Qim多享受一些美好时光....

Child-rearing is a journey, and you’ve only taken the first step. There’s still so much more to do!

rows.original: It’s a relief to know that the egg was laid without any complications, and that you should expect a healthy kip not unlike the clutch you already have. The kip is healthy, but it won’t incubate until you’re ready to be there with it; you just need to remember to come back. [var0|[flurry.name]|[frostwyrm.name]] heaves a heavy sigh through [var0|his|her] nose, [var0|his|her] nostrils flaring as the air rushes out of them. I understand that there are necessities that require your attention elsewhere, my Qal, [var0|he|she] says as [var0|he|she] leans down to nuzzle you. Return when you can.
rows.translation: 得知蛋顺利产下、没有出现任何并发症，而且可以期待一只和你现有窝中幼崽一样健康的小家伙，实在令人宽慰。幼崽很健康，但只有等你准备好陪在它身边时才会开始孵化；你只需要记得回来。 [var0|[flurry.name]|[frostwyrm.name]]从[var0|his|her]的鼻间发出一声沉重的叹息，气流喷涌而出，令[var0|his|her]的鼻孔张开。我明白，你还有必须去别处处理的事务，我的Qal，[var0|he|she]说道，同时[var0|he|she]俯身依偎着你。方便时就回来吧。

rows.original: You’re standing before Hana, whom is working the bar. A huskar like most of the locals, she’s surprisingly tall and willowy in stature despite her older, maternal appearance, making her curvy waist line and immodest bosom subtle in her silhouette. Beyond her mere figure the woman is raven haired, the black strands framing her head in a bob cut with a bang hanging across the side of her face, concealing the black, simplistic eyepatch over her right eye in the process. The usual ausar fur lines her arms and, you presume, her legs - though you can’t see the latter through the bar.
rows.translation: 你站在正在吧台后忙碌的哈娜面前。与当地大多数居民一样，她是个哈斯卡人。尽管外表年长、颇具母性，她的身材却出乎意料地高挑纤细，使得曲线优美的腰身和毫不含蓄的丰胸在整体轮廓中并不张扬。除了这副身材，女人还有一头乌黑秀发，黑色发丝剪成齐耳短发，环绕着她的头部，一绺刘海垂过侧脸，恰好遮住右眼上那只朴素的黑色眼罩。她的双臂覆着典型的奥萨人毛发，想必双腿也是如此 - 只是隔着吧台，你看不到后者。
rows.raw: "You’re standing before Hana, whom is working the bar. A huskar like most of the locals, she’s surprisingly tall and willowy in stature despite her older, maternal appearance, making her curvy waist line and immodest bosom subtle in her silhouette. Beyond her mere figure the woman is raven haired, the black strands framing her head in a bob cut with a bang hanging across the side of her face, concealing the black, simplistic eyepatch over her right eye in the process. The usual ausar fur lines her arms and, you presume, her legs - though you can’t see the latter through the bar."

rows.original: Unlike typical ausar, though, she also has fur puffing up around her neckline as if she is wearing a particularly fluffy scarf or shawl, given her huskar nature. All of the fur is black, but you can see a few aging gray strands stand out both in her hair and fuzzier fur. To accentuate this, or simply to avoid being too warm, the beige, cozy and body hugging wool sweater she wears opens in the chest, though where there’d be cleavage on any other woman lies a massive puff of fur overshadowing it
rows.translation: 不过，与典型的奥萨人不同，身为哈斯卡人的她颈部周围还蓬着一圈毛，仿佛围了一条格外蓬松的围巾或披肩。她全身的毛发都是黑色的，但无论头发还是更加绒密的兽毛中，都能看见几缕因年岁增长而格外显眼的灰白毛发。或许是为了衬托这一点，又或许只是为了避免太过暖和，她穿着一件米色、舒适且贴身的羊毛衫，胸前敞开；然而其他女人本该露出乳沟的位置，却被一大团蓬松毛发彻底遮住

rows.original: Hana is certainly the older sort, giving off a maternal sort of vibe from her appearance. However, her terse acting, unsmiling demeanor goes against the body image. As you’re eyeballing her she’s quietly watching you in the corner of her single eye as she otherwise works, cleaning mugs out with a thick looking cloth that hums with some technological purpose. While the barkeep is certainly waiting to serve you, it doesn’t look like she’s about to say something first.
rows.translation: 哈娜显然上了些年纪，外表散发着一种母性的气质。然而，她寡言的举止和不苟言笑的神态却与这副形象背道而驰。你打量她时，她仍在忙手头的工作，只以仅剩那只眼睛的余光静静观察着你；她正拿一块看起来很厚的布清洁酒杯，那块布发出嗡嗡声，显然有某种科技用途。酒保无疑正等着招待你，但她看起来并不打算先开口。

As you’re eyeballing her she’s quietly watching you in the corner of her single eye as she otherwise works, cleaning mugs out with a thick looking cloth that hums with some technological purpose. While the barkeep is certainly waiting to serve you, it doesn’t look like she’s about to say something first."

rows.original: “Well, I wouldn’t mind a drink.” You quip, leaning against the wood stained bartop expectantly.
rows.translation: “嗯，我倒不介意来一杯。”你打趣道，满怀期待地倚在染过色的木质吧台上。
rows.raw: "“Well, I wouldn’t mind a drink.” You quip, leaning against the wood stained bartop expectantly."

rows.original: Hana merely nods her head and lifts a hand away from her rag to tap at some interface hidden away beneath the bar, silently. Your codex chirps soon after with the menu - after a brief permission prompt, anyway. It’s surprisingly robust, so much so that you spend a good minute or so just flicking through the multitude of menus. Some of it also gets prohibitively expensive, too, but you’ve come to expect that with some esoteric vintages. Quietly you narrow down the listings in your head, ready to make an easy order.
rows.translation: 哈娜只是点点头，无言地把一只手从抹布上移开，在吧台下方某个藏起来的界面上轻点几下。片刻后，你的终端响了一声，显示出菜单 - 当然，之前还弹出了一个简短的权限提示。菜单的内容丰富得出人意料，以至于你光是在众多分类间翻看就花了足足一分钟左右。其中一些酒的价格也高得令人望而却步，不过对于某些稀奇的陈年佳酿，你已经见怪不怪了。你默默在心中缩小选择范围，准备轻松下单。
rows.raw: "\n\nHana merely nods her head and lifts a hand away from her rag to tap at some interface hidden away beneath the bar, silently. Your codex chirps soon after with the menu - after a brief permission prompt, anyway. It’s surprisingly robust, so much so that you spend a good minute or so just flicking through the multitude of menus. Some of it also gets prohibitively expensive, too, but you’ve come to expect that with some esoteric vintages. Quietly you narrow down the listings in your head, ready to make an easy order."

rows.translation: 蜂蜜酒
