rows.original: “What brings an exotic bird like you to this cold little moon?” Grimald giggles. “I was born here, silly! I’m a strong lad fresh from the Stormguard’s barracks,” the little guy boasts, like a peacock three times his size. “My family’s been on Uveto since the tenth Planet Rush. Well, my mother’s side of the family to be exact. We can trace our lineage back to the first settlers that made contact with this beautiful place’s friendly and not-so-friendly locals. As for my father, he’s an impressive anat. You might have crossed him in Uveto station. He works with the Camarilla, doing fancy stuff like coordinating ore trade between the empire and the tove.” “So you are a half-breed?” you ask. “Yes, half-anat, half-human. A very fluffy boy if you will,” he teases, waddling in his thic[silly |c |k ], stuffed parka. “My parents met near the radio tower, in the middle of a tribal truce. A truce that turned into a brawl. A drunk milodan chief presumably punched a korgonne envoy who then fell onto my Mom and shit hit the fan. In the blink of an eye, everyone was involved in the melee: Mom’s squad, Dad’s colleagues, local goons; absolutely everyone had a part in this deluge of unrestrained violence. My parents ended up back-to-back, surrounded by enraged korgonnes, with only a depowered thunder lance and a [silly |foldable chair |brutish goad ] left. According to Mom, it was [silly |but a tuesday |a nice challenge ]. As for Dad, it was the closest he was to dying. It was supposed to be a mundane peace agreement between the Camarilla and the western tribes, and it turned crazy.” At least they managed to leave unscathed. Did they get along well afterward? The amber-feathered boy nods. “Mom was impressed by my father’s insane bravery. For her — the fearsome zealot that modded herself to look like a divinely winged maiden — he wasn’t a puny bureaucrat unworthy of her attention anymore. Once the bloody mess was dealt with, she invited him for a quick drink at the Freezer. One thing led to another, they went on a date, then two, then settled together, got married, and had their first child.” You? “No, my big sister, Dahlia. She took a lot more than I did from Father. You wouldn’t differentiate her from a purebreed anat female except for her chestnut eyes. I was more like a happy little accident,” he laughs, this time a bit more dryly. You were not wanted? Grimald sighs. “Let’s just say I wasn’t the perfect boy they expected. They were very demanding. My sister and I had to be the best, no matter how hard it was. I’m lucky Dahlia shielded me from the worst of their misplaced pride and high standards. Fortunately, she excelled way over their expectations. She even got a scholarship for a famous Ausaril college. I, on the other hand, was meeker and shyer. Mom trained me to be a stormguard — which I became eventually, albeit after years in the Terran Space Coalition. But that’s a story for another time,” he says, looking at his augmented arms. Yeah, you can understand what he went through; your Dad and Briget pushed you a lot to become the [pc.race] you are now. Does he have a partner yet? “Interested in me, are you?” he teases before [flags.GRIMALD_SEX |winking at you |kissing you softly ]. “I’m not taken at the moment. Life’s been a bit too busy for that, but I hope to get there one day. I’m sure Mom will melt on the spot knowing I found a mate. She was over the moon when Dahlia presented Sloan, her essyra crush, to her. Can you imagine that? An amazonian valkyrie squealing in front of [silly |an extra thicc |a plus size ] vulpine huntress? Sloan’s cheeks were scarlet from embarrassment, and my sister’s teasing didn’t help. Whenever they are around, Dahlia gropes and praises her spouse in public. Stars, my sister’s a real freak.” She sounds interesting, that’s for sure. His family sounds weird, but the good kind of weird. Since you are on the topic of personal stuff, what does he like? The avian halfbreed smiles. “I really love hot chocolate and candied nuts, as you can see,” he says, raising his fuming cup. “I’m fond of the snow, of how the wind blows in my feathers when the sun sets, of how beautiful the sky looks whenever our distant star grants us a shimmering aurora. I love to pilot vehicles: be it a power-forklift, a vintage hoverbike, or a high-class pleasure yacht, I just love to be in control of a roaring engine. I wasn’t capable of flight for a very long time, so it was the closest I got to experiencing it. Stars, I’d kill to get my hands on our StormRider Skimmer; it’s a large, boat-like hovertank the Stormguard used back when we didn’t have train stations linking the savicite mines and harbors to Irestead. I bet it’s like driving a massive hovertank that’s as deft, fast, and agile as an eagle. At least Sloan lets me ride her kor’diiak when she’s in town. He’s so big and fluffy, a giant teddy bear like his mistress. I’ll try to tame one the next time she invites us to her place.” Is there anything he likes that isn’t related to speed? “I’m also a pretty good belly dancer. Sure, I love to pitch and catch, but I’m not one to do tantric acrobatics. I’m rather greedy in terms of nuts though. The more the merrier. I can’t get enough of fresh, alien seed. I’m not well-hung so I’m used to bottoming a lot. I also love getting praised and teased. Stars, I’m so sensitive down there, you won’t believe it without having a sample,” he says before realizing just how much he disclosed about his sex life. He blushes deeply, so flustered he hides his face in his fuzzy clothes. “Sorry sorry, I got a little carried away.” So he likes to be showered in sticky stuff and treated like the good boy he is? You’ll keep that in mind. Grimald slowly sips some hot chocolate, trying to calm himself a little. “I-I’m not just a sub. I can top too! I might not have the meatiest of sausages, but I’ve got balls to make an alpha dzaan blush. Else, I can show you just how cool it feels to play with hot stuff...” Now you see the stormguard in him shining. rows.translation: “像你这样充满异域风情的小鸟，怎么会来到这颗冰冷的小卫星？” 格里马尔德咯咯笑了起来。“我就出生在这里，傻瓜！我是刚从风暴卫士兵营出来的强壮小伙，”这个小家伙吹嘘道，活像一只体型比他大三倍的孔雀。“从第十次行星淘金热开始，我家就住在乌维托了。确切地说，是我母亲那边的家族。我们的血脉可以一直追溯到最初那批定居者，他们曾与这片美丽土地上友好和不那么友好的当地人接触。至于我父亲，他是位了不起的安纳泰。你或许在乌维托空间站见过他。他为秘党工作，负责协调帝国与托维族之间的矿石贸易之类的高端事务。” “所以你是混血儿？”你问道。 “对，一半安纳泰，一半人类。你也可以说我是个毛茸茸的男孩，”他调笑着，套着厚[silly |得离谱 |实 ]的填充派克大衣，摇摇摆摆地走动。“我父母是在无线电塔附近认识的，当时正值一场部落停战谈判。结果停战变成了群殴。据说是一名喝醉的米洛丹酋长揍了科尔贡使者一拳，后者又摔到我妈身上，于是场面彻底失控。转眼之间，所有人都卷进了混战：我妈的小队、我爸的同事、当地的打手；那场毫无节制的暴力洪流里，绝对人人都有份。我父母最后背靠着背，被愤怒的科尔贡人团团包围，手里只剩下一把没电的雷霆长枪和一把[silly |折叠椅 |粗野刺棒 ]。按我妈的说法，那不过是[silly |一个平平无奇的星期二 |一场不错的挑战 ]。可对我爸来说，那是他离死亡最近的一次。本来只是秘党与西部部落之间一场普通的和平协议，结果却彻底疯了。” 至少他们毫发无伤地脱身了。之后他们相处得好吗？ 琥珀色羽毛的男孩点点头。“我妈被我父亲那近乎疯狂的勇气打动了。对她这个把自己改造成神圣翼女模样的可怕狂信徒而言，他不再是个不值得她注意的软弱官僚。那场血腥混乱处理完后，她邀请他去冷冻库喝一杯。之后事情顺理成章，他们约了一次会，又约了第二次，接着同居、结婚，并生下了第一个孩子。” 是你？ “不，是我姐姐达莉娅。她继承父亲的特征比我多得多。除了栗色眼睛，你根本分辨不出她和纯血安纳泰女性有什么不同。而我更像是个令人开心的小意外，”他笑了笑，这次的笑声稍显干涩。 你不在他们的计划之中？ 格里马尔德叹了口气。“这么说吧，我不是他们期望中的完美男孩。他们要求非常严格。无论有多难，我和姐姐都必须做到最好。幸好达莉娅替我挡下了他们错位的骄傲和过高标准所带来的最坏影响。幸运的是，她的表现远远超过他们的期望，甚至获得奖学金，进入一所著名的奥萨瑞尔学院。而我则更温顺、更害羞。妈妈把我训练成风暴卫士——我最终确实成为了风暴卫士，尽管此前在地球人太空联盟待了很多年。不过，那是另一个故事了，”他说着，看向自己经过强化的双臂。 嗯，你能理解他的经历；爸爸和布里吉特也曾不断鞭策你，才让你成为如今这样的[pc.race]。那么，他现在有伴侣吗？ “你对我有兴趣，是吗？”他调笑道，随后[flags.GRIMALD_SEX |朝你眨了眨眼 |轻柔地吻了你 ]。“我目前还是单身。生活一直有点太忙，顾不上这些，不过我希望总有一天能找到伴侣。我妈要是知道我找到了配偶，肯定会当场融化。达莉娅把她迷恋的艾西拉人斯隆介绍给她时，她简直欣喜若狂。你能想象吗？一个亚马逊女武神在一名[silly |格外丰腴的 |大码的 ]狐族女猎手面前尖叫？斯隆尴尬得双颊通红，我姐姐还一个劲地逗她。只要她们待在一起，达莉娅就会当众抚摸并夸奖自己的配偶。星辰在上，我姐姐真是个变态。” 她听起来确实很有意思。他的家人听起来很怪，但属于讨人喜欢的那种怪。既然聊到了私人话题，他喜欢什么？ 这名鸟族混血儿笑了。“我真的很喜欢热巧克力和糖渍坚果，你也看得出来，”他说着，举起冒着热气的杯子。“我喜欢雪，喜欢夕阳西下时风吹过羽毛的感觉，也喜欢遥远恒星赐予我们闪耀极光时，天空呈现出的美景。我热爱驾驶载具：无论是动力叉车、老式悬浮摩托，还是高档豪华游艇，我就是喜欢掌控轰鸣引擎的感觉。我曾经很长时间都无法飞行，所以驾驶载具是最接近飞翔的体验。星辰在上，要是能让我驾驶风暴骑手掠行艇，我愿意为此拼命；那是一种船形的大型悬浮坦克，早在铁路尚未把萨维石矿场和港口与艾尔斯泰德连接起来时，风暴卫士就用它通行。我敢说，驾驶它就像操纵一辆庞大的悬浮坦克，却又像雄鹰一样灵巧、迅捷、敏锐。至少斯隆进城时会让我骑她的科尔迪亚克。它又大又毛茸茸的，就像它的女主人一样，是只巨型泰迪熊。下次她邀请我们去她那里时，我也要试着驯服一只。” 他有没有什么与速度无关的爱好？ “我的肚皮舞也跳得相当不错。妈妈不希望我做这么娘娘腔的事，但我还是设法在一次次任务之间东学一点、西学一点。你要是愿意，我可以为你单独表演，”他调笑道。 “单独表演？你不觉得自己飞得离太阳太近了吗？” “我绝不会飞得太近，不过如果你哪天想和小鸟上床，得知道我没那么重口。没错，我能攻也能受，但我不喜欢做什么密宗杂技。说到坚果，我倒是相当贪心，越多越好。新鲜的外星精液我怎么都吃不够。我的家伙不算大，所以早就习惯在下面了。我也喜欢被夸奖和调戏。星辰在上，我下面敏感得要命，不亲自尝试一下你绝对不会相信，”他说完才意识到，自己透露了多少性生活细节。他脸红得厉害，慌乱到把脸埋进毛茸茸的衣服里。“对不起，对不起，我有点说过头了。” 所以，他喜欢浑身沾满黏糊糊的东西，还喜欢被当成乖孩子对待？你会记住的。格里马尔德慢慢啜饮热巧克力，努力让自己平静一些。 “我、我不只是个受。我也能当攻！我的香肠或许不是最粗壮的，但我的蛋蛋足以让一个德赞阿尔法都脸红。不然，我也可以让你见识一下玩火热东西有多爽...” 现在你终于看见了他身为风暴卫士的一面。只要他能跟上你，和一只神话般的雷鸟玩玩也不会太糟。 格里马尔德叹了口气。“[flags.GRIMALD_SEX |只是请别把我的羽毛弄得太乱 |记得轻柔地对待我的羽毛 ]。它们非常敏感，而且清理起来要花很长时间[silly | D: |。 ]”

rows.original: “You are working for the Stormguard, correct?” The cute boy nods. “Yep. I’m in the third recon team, the medical intervention and emergency rescue squad. If one of us or somebody that booked our services is in dire need of extraction, we must be ready to scour the tundra, glacier, and even the glacial ocean to find them,” he proudly boasts, making his feathery tail sway behind him. Interesting. “Is it your first job? You look rather young, after all.” “Don’t let my cute face fool you. I’m a big boy: a veteran from the Terran Space Coalition’s fleet.” “Wait, you were in the [silly |Navy |Terran forces ]?” you ask, a bit shocked. “You had the galaxy to explore and you landed here of all places?” Grimald sips some hot chocolate. “Uveto is my homeworld, so it’s not that weird I came back here when I was demobilized. Being in the army was fun. I had lots of free time between ship maintenance, I learned field medic and surgeon skills, and the boys and gals were so chill compared to, well, my parents.” [var0 |You understand. Vic and Briget were also strict and tough with you. But it’s still concerning that his mother and father were stricter than the peacekeeping forces! |The peacekeeping forces had more lenient rules than his parents? He must have had a very strict upbringing! ] “You can’t help it. With a mother in the Stormguard and a father from the Anat Empire, you will have a very demanding schooling. It wasn’t so bad though; in comparison, my time in the army seemed more like a vacation with easy classes from time to time. I even became my ship’s most talented performer. Stars, I loved ceremonial parades and going out on permission with my friends. I spent many days and nights dancing half-naked on top of bar tables, swaying my feathers like a peacock. Everyone called me Chou Chou behind closed doors – and under weighted blankets,” he winks. Well, it sounds like he had a very good time being a soldier. Why did he leave? The avian femboy frowns and raises his right arm. You easily spot the circuitry and hardlight devices laced in his modded flesh. There’s also tiny white scars scattered here and there, almost invisible from afar. “My ship, the Rhadamanthus, escorted a convoy through a recently-secured quadrant. We knew this wouldn’t be a pleasant ride and that we would come across pirates, but since we had three escort ships flanking our spacecraft carrier, we knew only the strongest or most reckless of them would even dare approach us. And they did: halfway through an asteroid field, they rose from the star’s fiery crown and from behind a gaseous planet’s moon at ramming speed, ready to engage us. We immediately recognized their flagship’s emblem: the Black Void.” How did they fare against them? “Badly. By the time we were harnessed and deployed around the convoy, they had already closed their jaws on us. We were trapped between the cold and a hard place, surrounded by three times more ships than we had. Let me just-” Grimald recovers a small holo-device from a hidden pocket and activates it. In the blink of an eye, a projection of a small star system and bundles of triangular tokens lights your surroundings. “Commander Nesm used the Rhadamanthus to shield the smaller transporters from the worst of the missiles, lasers, and thermal cannons blasts,” he says as swarms of small ships surround the biggest vessel. “I lost many friends, but we made them bleed far more,” he mumbles, his face suddenly somber and hurt. “Since we knew conventional maneuvers wouldn’t suffice to push them back, we improvised and used the asteroid fields as hunting grounds,” he says. Meanwhile, the holographic ships sail through the spatial reef. “Between the uneven gravitic disturbances and the deluge of missiles unleashed upon us, it’s a miracle so many pilots survived the raid – even more that so many were mostly unscathed.” But he wasn’t one of them, right? The amber-feathered stormguard nods. “I was a bomber pilot, so I was slower and took way more flak than others,” he replies, pointing at one of the tiny points skittering toward the pirate battleships. “I barely had the time to fire electromagnetic torpedoes at our enemies’ bulkiest cruiser before a lumpy corvette hit me with its coil cannons. My shields broke and I felt something sting my arms, but I didn’t see anything. Since we couldn’t afford to lose what little armor-piercing capabilities the fleet had, I continued to fight with a growing ache in my hands, firing my [silly |lazor |ordnance ] in the hope of crippling them with a direct hit to a reactor or thruster. Luckily for us, a patrolling fleet arrived in the system at the right moment.” “The Black Void might be organized and have a rigid, almost military structure, but they remain outlaws, and outlaws are innately selfish. Their troops’ coherency crumbled, which allowed us to easily cripple their biggest ships. It was a bitter victory, but this could have been far worse. Fighting the debilitating pain, I landed on the Rhadamanthus and was immediately taken by the crew’s medics. I didn’t understand at the time because of the adrenaline, but I was on the verge of losing my arms.” Losing his arms? Was it because of the corvette’s blow? “I did lose them in some way. My nerves and ligaments were almost severed by minuscule, subatomic debris, and the long space fight didn’t help. Thousands of tiny needles pierced my flesh and bones. What makes it a particularly vicious weapon is that they slowly dissolve with time, taking skin, bones, ligaments, and muscles with them. The medical crew operated on me in an emergency, between a badly-burned kaithrit and an officer crushed by a command console. In the end, the surgeons replaced about eighty percent of my hands’ flesh and bones with cybernetics. My left thumb is the only finger attached to a fleshy muscle for instance, while most of my right side is fine flesh-wise but my bones were all replaced. They did a great job fixing me, considering the situation at the time and what little means they had. I used a fair share of my savings to add hardlight feathers projectors to them – I didn’t want people to look at my arms and be sad, especially since I was the cheerful one; the one entertaining others and putting a smile on people’s faces.” So after this accident, he was demobilized and returned to Uveto? “My contract came to an end two weeks after I left the medical bay, and I didn’t plan to stay much longer anyway. I made a promise to one of my comrades: to stay the same, happy ray of sunshine no matter what and to always follow my heart. So I took my disability pension and returned home for the first time in three years. Mom hugged me for five minutes straight when I showed up with my snow-covered uniform. At the time, they were looking for a new pilot to drive the recovery shuttle, so I applied for the position and passed with flying colors,” he proudly boasts. What does his job entail? Does he have to do only ship-related tasks or does he need to fight as well? The harpy boy shrugs. “A bit of both. I need to be ready to fight anything that threatens my fellow stormguards’ integrity. Since I’m the medical team’s pilot, I need to know how to drive carefully and quickly enough to bring people back to safety and heal them before they either die from their wounds or freeze to death. It’s not unusual for my colleagues to operate on people in the middle of a flight. It’s rather bone-chilling to know that you might have either been too slow to save them from the cold or too fast to allow them to perform emergency procedures.” Does it happen often? “Not really, no. Most of the time, we are called to rescue somebody from the blizzard or to transport tourists back to Irestead’s dispensary after a bad fall. It’s rare that we need to do surgery on the spot. Discovering the true state of our patient is always a surprise — and usually not a pleasant one. You know it’ll be a long day when you reach for the heavy duty tools before the litter.” Did he have to operate somebody on the glacier? Grimald nods. “Once. The alpha team was greatly injured and needed to be evacuated immediately. It was dark and the blizzard was dense. They didn’t realize they were into Kor’diiak hunting grounds before the mighty beasts surrounded them. No matter how strong and tough you are, you are no match against an ursus gigantus — let alone eight of them.” “Two stormguards, Ymgir and Fjoor, were in pretty bad shape. The alien bears focused on them because they were the shortest and bulkiest of the squad. The former, a dwarfish huskar, needed oxygen after one of the apex predators collapsed on him while his gigantic companion took the worst of their punishment defending him. To this day, I don’t know how we managed to lift the kor’diiak off Ymgir, let alone stabilize Fjorr. I only remember red blotches and my racing breaths turning into wet clouds. It took us an hour of desperate work to be able to move him back to the ship. Nobody in the medical team slept until they both awakened in the dispensary. It’s a miracle they got away with just a few scars and broken bones.” All’s well that ends well. After all, they were in very good hands. “S-Sure,” Grimald replies, blushing slightly. “I’ve still room to improve but even I was surprised I could perform so well under pressure. My arms might be mostly artificial, but the work they can do is genuine.” What does he do when he isn’t dispatched? “I usually spend time polishing the shuttle’s sides, rigging the antigrav engine, checking the onboard medic kits, and waiting for an emergency call. We’ve got one or two per week on average, but we aren’t safe from a brutal avalanche or a mining shaft accident. There’s also the more mundane incidents like exhibitionism or bar brawls, but I usually take care of the aftermath.” “Exhibitionism? In this climate?” Grimald giggles. “It’s more likely than you’d think. Between the sauna users thinking they’re invincible or drunkards that got one too many glasses at the Freezer, we’ve got a lot of work to do. We usually arrive before the sheriff, not that they can do much against the cold. A quick sip of firewater, a warm coat, and a heat belt usually suffice to fix the problem, but it’s good to have the sobering cells at hand. Our hold is more of a fancy monastery than a proper police station or hospital. We do, however, have nice kitchens and delicious roasted meats,” he says, clearly not thinking about food. Did he get in one of his friends’ pants? “Not yet,” he replies, hiding his blushing cheeks behind his mug. “Relations between members of the same teams aren’t forbidden, but we are enticed to spread and reproduce if you know what I mean. Stars, there’s so many hung dudes and chesty gals in here. You should see our sexy calendars... and the showers! Oh, the communal showers!” You cough, stopping the little bird’s daydreaming. The small bulge in his trousers twitches through his layered fabric. “I see your ship isn’t the only thing you polish.” “I’d love to have some fun sometimes. No matter how fine the snow is and how good the chocolate tastes, the nights are still long and cold, albeit beautiful. One day, I’ll find my special someone. Somebody who’ll hold me tight against them, give me a kiss before going to work, and help me groom my feathers. For someone like that, I’d do anything, even give them my arms.” “How would you even fly without them?” you retort. Grimald smirks. “I wouldn’t be against being a househusband, but my team will surely miss me. Some knew me since the cradle. I’m almost a nephew to the main medical officer. He told me multiple times he’d like me to finish my studies to take his place when the time comes. I’m not ready yet to return to school — and don’t have the funds for it — so that settles the issue for now, but I wouldn’t be against having a better degree than my sister. Until then, I’ll remain a fine pilot and field medic.”
rows.translation: “你是在为风暴卫士工作，对吧？” 这个可爱的男孩点点头。“没错。我在第三侦察队，也就是医疗干预与紧急救援小队。如果我们的人或雇用我们服务的人急需撤离，我们就必须做好搜遍苔原、冰川，乃至冰海也要找到他们的准备，”他自豪地夸耀道，身后的羽毛尾巴也随之摇摆起来。 有意思。“这是你的第一份工作吗？毕竟你看起来相当年轻。” “别被我可爱的脸蛋骗了。我可是个大男孩：还是地球太空联盟舰队的老兵呢。” “等等，你以前在[silly |海军 |地球部队 ]服役？”你有些震惊地问。“整片银河都任你探索，结果你偏偏落脚到了这里？” 格里马尔德啜饮了一口热巧克力。“乌维托是我的母星，所以复员后回到这里也没那么奇怪。在军队里的日子挺有趣的。舰船维护工作之间有很多空闲时间，我学会了战地医护和外科技能，而且那些男男女女都很随和，至少跟我父母比起来是这样。” [var0 |你能理解。维克和布里吉特以前对你也很严厉强硬。不过，他的父母居然比维和部队还严格，还是让人有些担忧！ |维和部队的规矩居然比他父母还宽松？他的家教肯定严厉得不得了！ ] “这也没办法。母亲是风暴卫士，父亲又来自安纳泰帝国，学业自然会被要求得非常严格。不过也不算太糟；相比之下，军旅生活简直像在度假，只是偶尔上几堂轻松的课。我甚至成了舰上最有才华的表演者。群星在上，我可喜欢仪仗游行，还有获准外出时跟朋友们一起玩了。我曾有许多个白天和夜晚半裸着在酒吧桌上跳舞，像孔雀一样摆动羽毛。私下里大家都叫我啾啾——尤其是在加重毯下面，”他眨了眨眼。 好吧，听起来他的军旅生活过得相当愉快。那他为什么离开了？ 这名鸟族伪娘皱起眉头，抬起右臂。你很容易便看见改造血肉中交织的电路与硬光装置。上面还散落着一道道细小的白色伤疤，从远处几乎看不出来。“我的舰船拉达曼图斯号当时护送一支船队穿越刚刚确保安全的星区。我们知道这趟旅程不会太平，也肯定会碰上海盗；不过既然有三艘护航舰分列航空母舰两侧，我们以为只有最强大或最鲁莽的家伙才敢靠近。结果他们真的来了：航程行至一片小行星带中途，他们从恒星炽烈的日冕中、又从一颗气态行星的卫星后方以冲撞速度杀出，准备与我们交战。我们立刻认出了旗舰上的徽记：黑色虚空。” 他们跟那些人交战的结果如何？ “很糟。等我们系好安全带、在船队周围部署完毕时，他们的利齿已经咬住了我们。我们被困在冰冷太空与硬茬之间，敌舰数量是我们的三倍，把我们团团包围。让我先——” 格里马尔德从隐藏口袋里取出一台小型全息装置并将其启动。转眼之间，一个小型恒星系的投影和一簇簇三角形标记便照亮了你们周围。“内斯姆指挥官用拉达曼图斯号替较小的运输舰挡下了最猛烈的导弹、激光和热能炮轰击，”他说着，一群小型舰船围住了最大的那艘船。 “我失去了许多朋友，但我们让他们流了更多血，”他喃喃说道，神情忽然变得阴郁而痛苦。“我们知道常规机动不足以击退他们，于是临机应变，把小行星带变成了猎场，”他说。与此同时，全息舰船正穿行在这片太空礁群之中。“不均匀的引力扰动，再加上朝我们倾泻而来的导弹，居然还有这么多飞行员在袭击中活了下来，简直是个奇迹——更别说其中许多人几乎毫发无伤。” 但他不是毫发无伤的那一个，对吧？ 这名琥珀色羽毛的风暴卫士点点头。“我是轰炸机飞行员，所以速度更慢，承受的防空火力也比其他人多得多，”他回答道，指着其中一个朝海盗战舰疾驰的小光点。“我才刚来得及向敌人最笨重的巡洋舰发射电磁鱼雷，一艘臃肿的轻型护卫舰就用线圈炮击中了我。护盾破裂，我感觉双臂像被什么东西刺了一下，却什么也没看到。舰队仅存的穿甲能力本就少得可怜，我们不能再失去它，所以我忍着双手越来越强烈的疼痛继续战斗，不断发射我的[silly |镭射炮 |弹药 ]，盼着能直接命中反应堆或推进器，让他们彻底瘫痪。幸运的是，一支巡逻舰队恰好在正确的时刻抵达了这个星系。” “黑色虚空或许组织严密，也有近乎军队般严格的架构，但他们终究是法外之徒，而法外之徒天性自私。他们部队的协同性随即崩溃，让我们得以轻易重创其最大的几艘舰船。那是一场苦涩的胜利，不过情况原本可能糟糕得多。我强忍着令人虚弱的疼痛降落在拉达曼图斯号上，立刻被舰员中的医护人员带走。由于肾上腺素作祟，我当时并不明白，自己其实已经到了失去双臂的边缘。” 失去双臂？是因为那艘轻型护卫舰的攻击吗？ “从某种意义上说，我确实失去了它们。细微到亚原子尺度的碎屑几乎切断了我的神经和韧带，而那场漫长的太空战斗更是雪上加霜。成千上万根细针刺穿了我的血肉与骨骼。这种武器格外恶毒的地方在于，那些碎屑会随着时间缓慢溶解，同时带走皮肤、骨骼、韧带和肌肉。医疗组在一名严重烧伤的凯斯里特人与一名被指挥控制台压伤的军官之间，紧急为我进行了手术。最终，外科医生用义体替换了我双手大约百分之八十的血肉与骨骼。比如说，我的左手拇指是唯一仍连接着血肉肌肉的手指；而右边大部分在血肉方面还算完好，但骨头已经全部换掉了。考虑到当时的情形和他们手头少得可怜的条件，他们把我修复得非常好。我花了不少积蓄给双臂加装硬光羽毛投影器——我不想让别人看到我的手臂就觉得难过，尤其因为我一直都是那个开朗的人；那个负责娱乐大家、让人们脸上露出笑容的人。” 所以事故过后，他就复员并返回乌维托了？ “我离开医务室两周后合同便到期了，反正我也没打算再待太久。我曾向一名战友保证：无论发生什么，都要做那个一如既往、快乐得像阳光一样的人，而且永远听从自己的内心。于是我领了伤残抚恤金，三年来第一次回到家乡。我穿着落满雪的制服出现在妈妈面前时，她足足抱了我五分钟。当时他们正在招募一名驾驶救援穿梭机的新飞行员，所以我申请了这个职位，并以优异成绩通过考核，”他自豪地说道。 他的工作具体包括什么？只需要负责舰船相关任务，还是也得参加战斗？ 这个哈比男孩耸耸肩。“两者都有一点。我必须随时准备对付任何威胁同伴风暴卫士人身安全的东西。身为医疗队的飞行员，我得懂得怎样既小心又足够迅速地驾驶，好把人们带回安全地带，并在他们因伤死亡或冻死之前救治他们。我的同事在飞行途中给人动手术并不少见。想到你可能是开得太慢，没能及时把人从严寒中救出来；也可能是开得太快，让他们来不及完成紧急处置，实在让人不寒而栗。” 这种情况经常发生吗？ “其实不会。大多数时候，我们只是接到呼叫，要从暴风雪里救人，或是在游客严重摔伤后把他们送回艾尔斯泰德的医务所。需要当场动手术的情况很少。患者的真实状况总会带来意外——而且通常不是什么愉快的意外。如果还没拿担架，你就先伸手去取重型工具，那你便知道这一天会很漫长。” 他有没有在冰川上给人做过手术？ 格里马尔德点点头。“有一次。阿尔法小队伤得很重，必须立刻撤离。当时天色漆黑，暴风雪又非常浓密。他们没有意识到自己闯进了科尔迪亚克的猎场，直到那些强大的野兽把他们包围。无论你多么强壮坚韧，都不可能是巨熊兽的对手——更别说一次面对八头。” “两名风暴卫士伊姆吉尔和菲约尔伤势相当严重。那些外星熊专门攻击他们，因为他们是小队里身材最矮、体格最敦实的两个人。前者是个矮人般的赫斯卡，一头顶级掠食者压倒在他身上后，他需要立刻吸氧；而他那位巨人般的同伴则为了保护他，承受了最猛烈的攻击。直到今天，我也不知道我们当时究竟是怎么把那头科尔迪亚克从伊姆吉尔身上抬开的，更别说稳住菲约尔的伤势了。我只记得一团团红色斑块，还有自己急促的呼吸化为湿润的白雾。我们拼命忙了一个小时，才终于能够把他移回舰船。在他们两人于医务所醒来之前，医疗队没有一个人睡觉。他们最后只留下几道伤疤和几处骨折，简直是个奇迹。” 结局好就一切都好。毕竟，他们当时可是由一双非常可靠的手照料着。 “当、当然，”格里马尔德回答，微微红了脸。“我还有很大的进步空间，不过连我自己都很惊讶，居然能在压力下表现得这么好。我的双臂大多是人造的，但它们完成的工作却货真价实。” 没有出勤任务时，他会做些什么？ “我通常会擦亮穿梭机的外壳，调校反重力引擎，检查舰载医疗包，然后等待紧急呼叫。平均每周会有一两次，不过我们也可能遇上猛烈的雪崩或矿井事故。还有一些更普通的事件，比如暴露癖或酒吧斗殴，但我一般只负责处理善后。” “暴露癖？在这种气候下？” 格里马尔德咯咯笑了起来。“这种事比你想象中更常见。桑拿使用者觉得自己无所不能，还有在冷冻库酒吧里多喝了几杯的醉鬼，这些人给我们带来了不少工作。我们通常比治安官先到，不过他们对寒冷也做不了多少事。快速喝一口烈性酒，披上一件暖和的外套，再戴上热能腰带，通常就足以解决问题；但手边有醒酒拘留室还是很方便。我们的要塞与其说是正规的警察局或医院，倒更像一座豪华修道院。不过我们的厨房很不错，烤肉也非常美味，”他说着，心里显然想的并不是食物。 他有没有钻进某个朋友的裤子里？ “还没有，”他回答，用马克杯遮住泛红的脸颊。“同队成员之间的关系并不受禁止，不过大家会被鼓励开枝散叶、繁衍后代，你明白我的意思吧。群星在上，这里有太多胯下雄伟的男人和胸部丰满的女人了。你真该看看我们的性感日历...还有淋浴间！噢，那些公共淋浴间！” 你咳了一声，打断这只小鸟的幻想。他裤子里的小小隆起隔着层层布料抽动了一下。“看来你擦亮的不只有舰船。” “我有时也很想找点乐子。不管雪有多么细腻，巧克力有多么香甜，夜晚依旧漫长而寒冷，尽管也很美丽。总有一天，我会找到那个特别的人。一个会把我紧紧搂在怀里、上班前亲吻我、还会帮我梳理羽毛的人。为了那样的人，我愿意做任何事，甚至把双臂都交给对方。” “没了手臂，你还怎么驾驶？”你反驳道。 格里马尔德得意一笑。“我倒不介意当家庭主夫，不过我的小队肯定会想念我。有些人从我还在摇篮里时就认识我了。对首席医疗官来说，我几乎就像他的外甥。他已经跟我说过很多次，希望我完成学业，等时机成熟后接替他的位置。我还没准备好重返学校——也没有足够的钱——所以目前这件事就先这样了，不过我倒不介意拿到比姐姐更高的学位。在那之前，我会继续当一名称职的飞行员和战地医护。”
rows.raw: " “You are working for the Stormguard, correct?” The cute boy nods. “Yep. I’m in the third recon team, the medical intervention and emergency rescue squad. If one of us or somebody that booked our services is in dire need of extraction, we must be ready to scour the tundra, glacier, and even the glacial ocean to find them,” he proudly boasts, making his feathery tail sway behind him. Interesting. “Is it your first job? You look rather young, after all.” “Don’t let my cute face fool you. I’m a big boy: a veteran from the Terran Space Coalition’s fleet.” “Wait, you were in the [silly |Navy |Terran forces ]?” you ask, a bit shocked. “You had the galaxy to explore and you landed here of all places?” Grimald sips some hot chocolate. “Uveto is my homeworld, so it’s not that weird I came back here when I was demobilized. Being in the army was fun. I had lots of free time between ship maintenance, I learned field medic and surgeon skills, and the boys and gals were so chill compared to, well, my parents.” [var0 |You understand. Vic and Briget were also strict and tough with you. But it’s still concerning that his mother and father were stricter than the peacekeeping forces! |The peacekeeping forces had more lenient rules than his parents? He must have had a very strict upbringing! ] “You can’t help it. With a mother in the Stormguard and a father from the Anat Empire, you will have a very demanding schooling. It wasn’t so bad though; in comparison, my time in the army seemed more like a vacation with easy classes from time to time. I even became my ship’s most talented performer. Stars, I loved ceremonial parades and going out on permission with my friends. I spent many days and nights dancing half-naked on top of bar tables, swaying my feathers like a peacock. Everyone called me Chou Chou behind closed doors – and under weighted blankets,” he winks. Well, it sounds like he had a very good time being a soldier. Why did he leave? The avian femboy frowns and raises his right arm. You easily spot the circuitry and hardlight devices laced in his modded flesh. There’s also tiny white scars scattered here and there, almost invisible from afar. “My ship, the Rhadamanthus, escorted a convoy through a recently-secured quadrant. We knew this wouldn’t be a pleasant ride and that we would come across pirates, but since we had three escort ships flanking our spacecraft carrier, we knew only the strongest or most reckless of them would even dare approach us. And they did: halfway through an asteroid field, they rose from the star’s fiery crown and from behind a gaseous planet’s moon at ramming speed, ready to engage us. We immediately recognized their flagship’s emblem: the Black Void.” How did they fare against them? “Badly. By the time we were harnessed and deployed around the convoy, they had already closed their jaws on us. We were trapped between the cold and a hard place, surrounded by three times more ships than we had. Let me just-” Grimald recovers a small holo-device from a hidden pocket and activates it. In the blink of an eye, a projection of a small star system and bundles of triangular tokens lights your surroundings. “Commander Nesm used the Rhadamanthus to shield the smaller transporters from the worst of the missiles, lasers, and thermal cannons blasts,” he says as swarms of small ships surround the biggest vessel. “I lost many friends, but we made them bleed far more,” he mumbles, his face suddenly somber and hurt. “Since we knew conventional maneuvers wouldn’t suffice to push them back, we improvised and used the asteroid fields as hunting grounds,” he says. Meanwhile, the holographic ships sail through the spatial reef. “Between the uneven gravitic disturbances and the deluge of missiles unleashed upon us, it’s a miracle so many pilots survived the raid – even more that so many were mostly unscathed.” But he wasn’t one of them, right? The amber-feathered stormguard nods. “I was a bomber pilot, so I was slower and took way more flak than others,” he replies, pointing at one of the tiny points skittering toward the pirate battleships. “I barely had the time to fire electromagnetic torpedoes at our enemies’ bulkiest cruiser before a lumpy corvette hit me with its coil cannons. My shields broke and I felt something sting my arms, but I didn’t see anything. Since we couldn’t afford to lose what little armor-piercing capabilities the fleet had, I continued to fight with a growing ache in my hands, firing my [silly |lazor |ordnance ] in the hope of crippling them with a direct hit to a reactor or thruster. Luckily for us, a patrolling fleet arrived in the system at the right moment.” “The Black Void might be organized and have a rigid, almost military structure, but they remain outlaws, and outlaws are innately selfish. Their troops’ coherency crumbled, which allowed us to easily cripple their biggest ships. It was a bitter victory, but this could have been far worse. Fighting the debilitating pain, I landed on the Rhadamanthus and was immediately taken by the crew’s medics. I didn’t understand at the time because of the adrenaline, but I was on the verge of losing my arms.” Losing his arms? Was it because of the corvette’s blow? “I did lose them in some way. My nerves and ligaments were almost severed by minuscule, subatomic debris, and the long space fight didn’t help. Thousands of tiny needles pierced my flesh and bones. What makes it a particularly vicious weapon is that they slowly dissolve with time, taking skin, bones, ligaments, and muscles with them. The medical crew operated on me in an emergency, between a badly-burned kaithrit and an officer crushed by a command console. In the end, the surgeons replaced about eighty percent of my hands’ flesh and bones with cybernetics. My left thumb is the only finger attached to a fleshy muscle for instance, while most of my right side is fine flesh-wise but my bones were all replaced. They did a great job fixing me, considering the situation at the time and what little means they had. I used a fair share of my savings to add hardlight feathers projectors to them – I didn’t want people to look at my arms and be sad, especially since I was the cheerful one; the one entertaining others and putting a smile on people’s faces.” So after this accident, he was demobilized and returned to Uveto? “My contract came to an end two weeks after I left the medical bay, and I didn’t plan to stay much longer anyway. I made a promise to one of my comrades: to stay the same, happy ray of sunshine no matter what and to always follow my heart. So I took my disability pension and returned home for the first time in three years. Mom hugged me for five minutes straight when I showed up with my snow-covered uniform. At the time, they were looking for a new pilot to drive the recovery shuttle, so I applied for the position and passed with flying colors,” he proudly boasts. What does his job entail? Does he have to do only ship-related tasks or does he need to fight as well? The harpy boy shrugs. “A bit of both. I need to be ready to fight anything that threatens my fellow stormguards’ integrity. Since I’m the medical team’s pilot, I need to know how to drive carefully and quickly enough to bring people back to safety and heal them before they either die from their wounds or freeze to death. It’s not unusual for my colleagues to operate on people in the middle of a flight. It’s rather bone-chilling to know that you might have either been too slow to save them from the cold or too fast to allow them to perform emergency procedures.” Does it happen often? “Not really, no. Most of the time, we are called to rescue somebody from the blizzard or to transport tourists back to Irestead’s dispensary after a bad fall. It’s rare that we need to do surgery on the spot. Discovering the true state of our patient is always a surprise — and usually not a pleasant one. You know it’ll be a long day when you reach for the heavy duty tools before the litter.” Did he have to operate somebody on the glacier? Grimald nods. “Once. The alpha team was greatly injured and needed to be evacuated immediately. It was dark and the blizzard was dense. They didn’t realize they were into Kor’diiak hunting grounds before the mighty beasts surrounded them. No matter how strong and tough you are, you are no match against an ursus gigantus — let alone eight of them.” “Two stormguards, Ymgir and Fjoor, were in pretty bad shape. The alien bears focused on them because they were the shortest and bulkiest of the squad. The former, a dwarfish huskar, needed oxygen after one of the apex predators collapsed on him while his gigantic companion took the worst of their punishment defending him. To this day, I don’t know how we managed to lift the kor’diiak off Ymgir, let alone stabilize Fjorr. I only remember red blotches and my racing breaths turning into wet clouds. It took us an hour of desperate work to be able to move him back to the ship. Nobody in the medical team slept until they both awakened in the dispensary. It’s a miracle they got away with just a few scars and broken bones.” All’s well that ends well. After all, they were in very good hands. “S-Sure,” Grimald replies, blushing slightly. “I’ve still room to improve but even I was surprised I could perform so well under pressure. My arms might be mostly artificial, but the work they can do is genuine.” What does he do when he isn’t dispatched? “I usually spend time polishing the shuttle’s sides, rigging the antigrav engine, checking the onboard medic kits, and waiting for an emergency call. We’ve got one or two per week on average, but we aren’t safe from a brutal avalanche or a mining shaft accident. There’s also the more mundane incidents like exhibitionism or bar brawls, but I usually take care of the aftermath.” “Exhibitionism? In this climate?” Grimald giggles. “It’s more likely than you’d think. Between the sauna users thinking they’re invincible or drunkards that got one too many glasses at the Freezer, we’ve got a lot of work to do. We usually arrive before the sheriff, not that they can do much against the cold. A quick sip of firewater, a warm coat, and a heat belt usually suffice to fix the problem, but it’s good to have the sobering cells at hand. Our hold is more of a fancy monastery than a proper police station or hospital. We do, however, have nice kitchens and delicious roasted meats,” he says, clearly not thinking about food. Did he get in one of his friends’ pants? “Not yet,” he replies, hiding his blushing cheeks behind his mug. “Relations between members of the same teams aren’t forbidden, but we are enticed to spread and reproduce if you know what I mean. Stars, there’s so many hung dudes and chesty gals in here. You should see our sexy calendars... and the showers! Oh, the communal showers!” You cough, stopping the little bird’s daydreaming. The small bulge in his trousers twitches through his layered fabric. “I see your ship isn’t the only thing you polish.” “I’d love to have some fun sometimes. No matter how fine the snow is and how good the chocolate tastes, the nights are still long and cold, albeit beautiful. One day, I’ll find my special someone. Somebody who’ll hold me tight against them, give me a kiss before going to work, and help me groom my feathers. For someone like that, I’d do anything, even give them my arms.” “How would you even fly without them?” you retort. Grimald smirks. “I wouldn’t be against being a househusband, but my team will surely miss me. Some knew me since the cradle. I’m almost a nephew to the main medical officer. He told me multiple times he’d like me to finish my studies to take his place when the time comes. I’m not ready yet to return to school — and don’t have the funds for it — so that settles the issue for now, but I wouldn’t be against having a better degree than my sister. Until then, I’ll remain a fine pilot and field medic.” "

rows.original: “What do you like about Uveto? There must be something special about this place that keeps you here.” The avian femboy sips some hot chocolate before answering. “There’s lots of things that make me feel at home here. First, there’s my family and childhood friends. You know how the saying goes: There’s no place like home. I’ve been to many places during my time in the terran fleet: Ausaril’s dry plains, Maggrath’s tropical jungles, Earth’s lush climate, Anon-Xusya B’s electromagnetic tempests, Dragarea’s volcanic hellscape, but nothing compares to my homeworld’s chill embrace. I liked Caphist — dad’s homeworld — too, but it’s not really the same. As much as I love the anat, their society makes my skin crawl.” How so? “Well... that they’re raised together, some not even knowing who their parents were. I know it helps them become their own person, but for someone who came from a nuclear family, I can’t understand how they build their identity without knowing their parents. A childhood friend of mine was adopted by an uplifted milodan couple. He was loved as much as his other siblings but he still needed to look for his biological parents, so I can only imagine how it must be for bevy-grown birdies.” You were raised mostly by Briget, but your parents were here when you needed them. You can understand him somewhat. Is there something he loves specifically about his family? Grimald thinks for a couple of seconds. “Mom used to bring us with her all around the moon. Dahlia, my sister, and I did lots of sledding and ice fishing with her. I remember the day we caught a forty pound anormalocaris. We unfortunately had to release the huge crustacean, but we brought a big scarlet cod home. Uveto has lots of arctic seafood, but most of the aquatic species are protected for scientific purposes. We don’t actually know which ones are at risk of extinction, because we only know a handful of them. The ecosystem is so rich, despite the rabid mining exploitation and the many problems it creates.” What was it like to grow up on Uveto? “It was fine. There were lots of snowball fights and snowman-building contests. I’m not very good at ice skating, but my sister was very skilled. She could have been a galactic champion if she wanted but she was more of a hockey player, with her broad shoulders and powerful legs. The Stormguard uses a good chunk of its credits to fund the sports team and school activities, to justify its social usefulness and buy themselves some respect from the less religious-inclined folks. There’s a yearly festival in Irestead with cheap local food, mead, games, and traditional music; tribal korgonne, milodans, and essyra usually participate as well and trade their goods with us.” Sounds fun. “That’s how my sister met her wife: they bumped together on the ice ring and she bought her a flask of thunderous firewater and cream-filled buns to apologize. I remember how Sloan’s cheeks turned crimson when Dahlia told her she’d like to taste essyra buns later.” “I see. Maybe I’ll need a date to guide me through the festival,” you tease, making his tail feathers sway happily behind him. “S-Sure. I also love how peaceful this place can be. The ice floe and tundra might be often scoured by blizzards and thunderstorms, but most of the time, only a dim breeze fills the empty plains and sharp canyons. When the sky’s clear, the starlight reflects on the layered ice and the frozen ores, turning the soil and mountains into an ethereal mix of colors. Legends say that when the fog settles and the glacier turns green, vengeful ghosts rise from the oceans below to drag travelers to their doom.” Are these stories true? Grimald shrugs. “No idea. I’ve been in one already but I saw no spirit or banshee. I did, however, rescue a stormguard warrior that wailed like one. Turns out she merely scratched her wrists, but her savicite piercings made her so sensitive that the slightest sting sufficed to trigger a masochistic trip in her pent-up mind. Pro tip: if you use savicite to enhance your psionic powers or to increase your bedroom fun, don’t forget to vent some steam; it’ll save you a very embarrassing visit to the doc. You wouldn’t believe what people use to relieve themselves when the green fever gets to them.” Did he, well... “No no no no. Fucking a delirious patient is out of question. We’ve got chill pills for preventive treatment and lucinite restraints for the most heat-addled minds. Nothing like a cool touch to quench the wildest of fires. Speaking of fiery events, we are approaching the aurora season. They are wonderful, especially when they reflect on the icy waters. The world looks like a kaleidoscopic swirl of colors. It’s absolutely mind-blowing. There’s even a spot where the electromagnetic waves interact with ancient pylons to create lightning jolts. It attracts lots of tourists.” [flags.PAULETTE_UVETO_DATE |“I saw them already with some friends. The sight was so magical from above.” “Above? You crossed the glacial canyons to get there? Only the bravest korgonne follow that path. You’re bolder or more reckless than I thought.” You smirk. “I like to live dangerously. And besides, I was well-escorted,” you tease, leaning closer to him. “Are there other places worthy of interest?” |“Are there other places of interest?” ] The male harpy thinks a little. “There’s the coral reefs and wonders of the depths if you aren’t scared of the dark – or from drowning. Some say an autonomous janeria colony claimed a lost depthsuit and now roams the ocean floor in search of targets to leech or, in the worst cases, assimilate. They’re only rumors, but it wouldn’t surprise me if they were true. For what it’s worth, there might be an entire underwater civilization under our feet. We barely scratched the surface of what’s under the planet’s icy crust, maybe there’s a hollow cavity between two layers of Uveto’s core.” It sounds unlikely. He talked about sledding earlier, does he have a favorite spot? “North-west of here, there’s a big, natural slope. Everyone from kids to old ones go there to ski, surf, and glide down the snowy canyon. There’s three tracks available: an easy one for beginners, an intermediate for seasoned riders, and a pro side for the bravest souls. It’s been a while since I went there, but I’d gladly take a free day to go there with [flags.GRIMALD_SEX |you, [pc.name] |a special someone ].” That sounds neat. You’ll think about it.
rows.translation: “你喜欢乌维托的哪些地方？这里一定有什么特别之处，才会让你留在这里吧。” 这位鸟族伪娘啜饮了一口热巧克力，随后回答。“有很多东西都让我觉得这里就是家。首先是我的家人和童年好友。你知道那句老话：金窝银窝，不如自己的狗窝。我在泰伦舰队服役时去过很多地方：奥萨里尔的干燥平原、马格拉斯的热带丛林、地球的葱郁气候、阿农-克苏亚B的电磁风暴、德拉加瑞亚的火山炼狱，但没有任何地方比得上故乡寒冷的怀抱。我也喜欢卡菲斯——爸爸的母星——但那里终究不一样。虽然我很喜欢阿纳特人，可他们的社会还是让我浑身不自在。” 怎么说？ “嗯...他们都是一起长大的，有些人甚至不知道自己的父母是谁。我知道这有助于他们成长为独立的个体，但对于在核心家庭中长大的我来说，我无法理解他们在不知道父母是谁的情况下要怎样建立自我认同。我有个童年好友被一对经过智能提升的米洛丹夫妻收养。他得到的爱并不比其他兄弟姐妹少，可他依旧需要寻找自己的亲生父母，所以我只能想象，在群育环境中长大的小鸟会是什么感受。” 你主要是由布丽吉特抚养长大的，不过当你需要父母时，他们也都在身边。你多少能理解他的感受。他有没有特别喜欢家人的某一点？ 格里马尔德思考了几秒。“妈妈以前常带着我们走遍这颗卫星。我的姐姐达莉娅和我经常跟她一起滑雪橇、冰钓。我还记得我们钓到一只四十磅重的奇虾那天。很遗憾，我们不得不放走那只巨大的甲壳动物，不过还是带了一条大红鳕鱼回家。乌维托有很多极地海产，但大多数水生物种都出于科研目的受到保护。我们其实不知道哪些物种正面临灭绝，因为我们了解的只有其中一小部分。尽管这里存在疯狂的采矿开发，以及由此引发的诸多问题，生态系统依然极其丰富。” 在乌维托长大是什么感觉？ “挺好的。这里经常打雪仗，也会举办堆雪人比赛。我不太擅长滑冰，不过我姐姐非常厉害。只要她愿意，本可以成为银河冠军，但她更喜欢打冰球，宽阔的肩膀和强健的双腿也很适合这项运动。风暴卫士会拿出相当一部分经费资助运动队和学校活动，以此证明自身的社会价值，并从那些不太信教的人手中买来几分尊重。艾尔斯特德每年都会举办节庆，那里有便宜的本地食物、蜂蜜酒、游戏和传统音乐；部落科尔贡、米洛丹和艾斯拉人通常也会参加，并和我们交换商品。” 听起来很有趣。 “我姐姐就是这样认识她妻子的：她们在冰场上撞到了一起，于是姐姐买了一壶雷鸣烈酒和几个奶油夹心面包向她道歉。我还记得，达莉娅说自己之后也想尝尝艾斯拉的‘面包’时，斯隆的脸颊一下子红透了。” “这样啊。也许我得找个约会对象带我逛逛节庆，”你调侃道，令他身后的尾羽愉快地摇摆起来。 “当、当然。我也喜欢这里能够如此宁静。浮冰和苔原虽然经常遭受暴风雪与雷暴侵袭，但大多数时候，空旷的平原和陡峭的峡谷间只有微风轻轻吹过。天空晴朗时，星光会映在层叠的冰层与冻结的矿石上，把大地和群山染成缥缈的斑斓色彩。传说当浓雾降临、冰川泛绿之时，复仇的幽灵便会从下方海洋中升起，把旅人拖向死亡。” 这些故事是真的吗？ 格里马尔德耸耸肩。“不知道。我已经遇到过一次那种雾，却没看见任何幽灵或女妖。不过，我倒是救过一名叫得像女妖一样的风暴卫士战士。结果她只是擦伤了手腕，但她身上的萨维石穿孔让她敏感得过了头，哪怕最轻微的刺痛，都足以在她压抑已久的脑海里触发一场受虐狂的迷幻之旅。专业建议：如果你用萨维石增强灵能力量，或者提高床上乐趣，别忘了定期释放一下；这样能免去一次极其尴尬的就诊。绿热病发作时，人们会拿什么东西来纾解欲望，你绝对想象不到。” 他该不会，那个... “不不不不。和神志不清的病人做爱绝对不行。我们有用于预防治疗的冷静丸，也有专门对付那些欲火焚心理智的露西石束具。再狂野的火焰，也没有什么是冰凉的触感浇不灭的。说到火热的景象，我们马上就要迎来极光季了。极光非常美，映照在冰冷水面上时尤其如此。整个世界看起来就像一团万花筒般旋转的色彩，绝对震撼心灵。甚至还有一处地方，电磁波会与古老的塔柱发生作用，制造出闪电冲击。那里吸引了许多游客。” [flags.PAULETTE_UVETO_DATE |“我已经和几个朋友一起看过了。从空中俯瞰时，那景色简直如梦似幻。” “空中？你穿过冰川峡谷去那里了？只有最勇敢的科尔贡人才会走那条路。看来你比我想象中更勇敢，或者更鲁莽。” 你坏笑起来。“我喜欢活得危险一点。而且，我当时有可靠的护卫，”你一边调侃，一边靠近他。“还有其他值得一看的地方吗？” |“还有其他值得一看的地方吗？” ] 这名男性鹰身人想了想。“如果你不怕黑，也不怕溺水，那还有珊瑚礁和深海奇观。有人说，一个自主生存的珍妮利亚群落占据了一套失落的深潜服，如今正在海底游荡，寻找可以吸取的目标，最糟糕的情况下还会把目标同化。这些只是传闻，但就算是真的，我也不会惊讶。说不定我们脚下存在着一整个水下文明。对于这颗星球冰壳之下的世界，我们才刚刚触及皮毛，也许乌维托核心的两层结构之间存在一个中空腔体。” 听起来不太可能。他之前提到过滑雪橇，那他有没有最喜欢的地点？ “从这里往西北走，有一片巨大的天然坡地。从孩子到老人，大家都会去那里滑雪、冲浪，沿着积雪的峡谷向下滑行。那里有三条路线：一条适合初学者的简单路线，一条适合老练滑手的中级路线，还有一条留给最勇敢者的专业路线。我已经很久没去过了，不过我很愿意抽出一天假期，和[flags.GRIMALD_SEX |你一起去，[pc.name] |某个特别的人一起去 ]。” 听起来不错。你会考虑的。

rows.original: “Do you get on well with Shade Irons?” Grimald raises an eyebrow. “Shade? I don’t know her as well as I’d like, to be sure. She isn’t among the most zealous and religious of the Stormguard, but that’s true of most of us. The clerical stuff is more like folklore than a real cult as of late. Mother never said anything bad about her. Considering how high her standards are, I guess it’s a good indicator on how well integrated Shade is. Why do you want to know, if I may ask?” Well... She’s very important to you, for personal reasons. “I see. I knew this snowkitty had a secret life,” he teases. “She’s a lucky woman. The old priest told me she was a mess when she arrived here years ago, but she quickly bulked up and became an impressive [silly |muscle milf |fighter ]. I don’t know what she does when she’s off-world, but it must be a high-risk, high-reward job, if her lifestyle is any indication. Her mate is also quite stunning. She isn’t here often, so Astra eagerly waits for her visits. Stars, when both of her parents are home, she’s so cheerful, her tail creates small whirlwinds behind her.” “Do you know her well?” The feathered femboy shakes his head. “Not that much, to be honest. We’re five years apart, so we didn’t grow up together in the pure sense of the term. I’ve seen her change a lot since I came back from the Terran Space Coalition’s fleet. She’s becoming more and more like a shieldmaiden of legends. Nobody carried her smashed or bruised to our medics, so either she’s shy and discrete or particularly level-headed and careful for her age — maybe both. I should ask Mom about her sometime. With some luck, she’ll be the top bitch in a handful of years.” The next chief of the Stormguard? Isn’t he exaggerating a little? “No, not the spiritual leader. The military acting leader. On the other hand,” he ponders, sipping on his mug, “warriors and mercenaries usually refuse to take positions of power because it implies less action and more paperwork. You wouldn’t believe how demanding handling all of the constant bullshit happening here and there is. Sometimes it feels like we’re managing a kindergarten, except the kids are over six feet tall and need a couple of drinks before their nap instead of a bedtime story. Multiple times, Mom came home fuming because her subordinates were too drunk to exercise or forget the basic arctic survival techniques. At least most of them are in good shape and remember their self-defense training when things get serious, else I’d be constantly on the move between the savicite mines, shores, and research facilities.” Fortunately, that’s not the case. Did he work with Shade already? The avian stormguard shakes his head again. “She does most of her business off-world, but I wouldn’t mind being her pilot. Stars, I’d love to test her MS-XI. According to my army friends, it’s a highly agile and fast vessel for its size and price. I wonder how she got her hands on it and if her contacts could get me a cheap one. Just thinking about flying a real spaceship again instead of a heavily-modified shuttle makes me all fuzzy. Don’t get me wrong, I adore the recon team’s transport, but it doesn’t compare to an Aegis-brand ship.”
rows.translation: “你和暗影·艾恩斯相处得好吗？” 格里马尔德挑起一边眉毛。“暗影？说实话，我对她的了解还没我希望的那么多。她不属于风暴卫士中最狂热、最虔诚的那一批，不过我们大多数人也都如此。近来那些教士规矩更像是民间传统，而非真正的宗教崇拜。母亲从没说过她的坏话。考虑到母亲的标准有多高，我想这足以说明暗影已经很好地融入了这里。恕我冒昧，你为什么想知道这些？” 这个嘛... 出于私人原因，她对你非常重要。 “我明白了。我就知道这只雪猫咪有着不为人知的生活，”他打趣道。“她可真幸运。老祭司告诉我，她几年前刚来这里时一团糟，不过很快就壮实起来，成了一位令人刮目相看的[silly |肌肉熟妇 |战士 ]。我不知道她离开这颗星球后做些什么，但从她的生活方式来看，那肯定是一份高风险、高回报的工作。她的伴侣也相当迷人。她不常来这里，所以阿斯特拉总是热切盼着她来访。星辰在上，当她的双亲都在家时，她高兴得不得了，尾巴能在身后刮起一阵阵小旋风。” “你很了解她吗？” 长着羽毛的伪娘摇了摇头。“说实话，不算很了解。我们相差五岁，所以严格来说并不是一起长大的。自从我从地球太空联盟的舰队回来后，我看着她改变了许多。她越来越像传说中的盾女了。没人把浑身是伤或满身瘀青的她抬到我们的医护人员面前，所以她要么害羞而低调，要么有着远超年龄的冷静与谨慎 — 也许两者兼有。我哪天应该问问母亲对她的看法。运气好的话，再过几年她就会成为这里最厉害的女战士。” 下一任风暴卫士首领？他是不是有点夸大了？ “不，不是精神领袖，而是军事上的代理统帅。话说回来，”他一边思索，一边啜饮杯中的饮料，“战士和佣兵通常不愿身居高位，因为那意味着行动更少、文书工作更多。你根本想象不到，要处理这里那里不断发生的种种破事有多费神。有时感觉我们像是在管理一所幼儿园，只不过这些孩子身高都超过六英尺，而且午睡前需要喝上几杯，而不是听睡前故事。母亲不止一次怒气冲冲地回家，因为她的部下醉得没法训练，或是忘了最基本的极地生存技巧。至少他们大多身体健壮，事情严重起来时也还记得自卫训练，否则我就得不停地在萨维晶矿场、海岸和研究设施之间来回奔波了。” 幸好情况并非如此。他以前和暗影共事过吗？ 这名鸟族风暴卫士再次摇了摇头。“她大部分工作都在外星进行，不过我不介意当她的飞行员。星辰在上，我真想试试她的MS-XI。军队里的朋友说，以它的尺寸和价格而言，那是一艘极其灵活而迅捷的飞船。我很好奇她是怎么弄到手的，也想知道她的人脉能不能替我搞来一艘便宜的。光是想到能再次驾驶真正的宇宙飞船，而不是一艘重度改装的穿梭机，我就兴奋得浑身发飘。别误会，我很喜欢侦察队的运输船，但它根本无法与神盾品牌的飞船相比。”

你靠近一些。“给我个惊喜。” 他笑了。“相信我，会非常甜。我去排队——能麻烦你在火边找个座位吗？” 刺骨寒意拍打着你的脸。没错，你会去找的。你可不想在这么冷的[dayNight |白天 |夜晚 ]排队。好在当地人在建筑沿线和饮食摊旁安装了硬光凉亭与火盆。你缓缓穿过稀疏的人群，寻找空位。[dayNight |小孩子们在雪地里玩耍，父母在远处看护。小科尔贡人与赫斯卡在年幼托夫和少数艾希拉的帮助下堆着雪人。小家伙们在雪雕上塑出大耳朵和长鼻子，用小小的双手挑战自然法则，创造出滑稽的嵌合兽和神话生物。全年都有雪一定很不错。 你渐渐放松下来，被这座极地城市迷住。阴险的寒意迫使你留在炽热的取暖点附近，但总体而言，你可以在这里待上几个小时。或许你可以买栋房子，度假时来住？附近甚至有个斯蒂尔科技前哨，若有紧急情况可以求助；艾妮克丝也住得不远，想找人陪伴时可以去见她。说到陪伴，格里马尔德已经离开一阵子了。希望他没事。 “[pc.name]？能、能帮个忙吗？” 你回头望去。格里马尔德不安地笑着。可怜的男孩用强化双手端着两杯饮料和满满一车热气腾腾的食物。你能看到微型活塞正奋力运作，维持手指紧握。你大发慈悲[pc.isAss |，难得一次 ]，从他手里接过一只杯子和一盘堆得冒尖的食物，放到附近桌上。野心勃勃的约会对象缓缓放下自己的饮料，小心地把为你买来的肉食和甜点一一取出。 “天啊，这也太多了！一定花了你一大笔钱！” 这只得意的鸟儿坏笑着。“我拿到了折扣——这里一半摊主以前都是我的同学。我给我们买了配李子蔓越莓酱的腌鲱鱼、浇融化奶酪的佐尔兽肉丸、配肉汁和奶酪的土豆泥、塞满洋葱、腌卷心菜与海豹培根的自制极地面包、配鳗鱼酱的斯塔克霍秋葵汤、酿南瓜、清蒸胡萝卜和豆子，还有[silly |甜面包卷 |蜂蜜姜饼 ].[flags.GRIMALD_HANGOUT | | 我不知道你是不是素食者，所以多拿了很多备用食物。 ]” “所有东西闻起来都好香。我们喝的是什么？”你问。 “[rand |加了米洛丹肉豆蔻的香料酒！别担心，酒精早就全蒸发了，喝起来很安全。 |驯鹿干汽水！这是用进口托夫水果制成的软饮料。味道非常特别，但和任何食物都很搭。 |艾尔斯泰德咖啡！这是奥萨咖啡，基底是南瓜糖浆，上面还加了鲜奶油和烘焙南瓜豆。我爸爸特别喜欢，尤其是滚烫的时候。 你喝了几口，随后开始享用多汁美食。能吃的东西实在太多，能探索的风味也太多了！你尽量保持均衡，既不太油腻，也不太清淡，就像布丽吉特教你的那样。格里马尔德狼吞虎咽地吃着面包和肉串，嘴里塞满油润肉食和裹满奶酪的土豆。半安纳泰人发现你在盯着他，顿时停了下来。 “对、对不起。我们早些时候遇到了紧急情况，我不得不错过晚餐。你尝过斯塔克霍秋葵汤了吗？斯塔克霍是一种小甲壳动物，以腐肉和深海生物牙缝里残留的肉屑为食。我知道听起来不怎么诱人，但它是真正的美味，尤其是配酿南瓜！” 你丝毫没有放心，但还是夹起一块浸满酱汁的肉咬了一口。他没撒谎，确实非常美味！这种虾状食物的酸味出乎意料，却与秋葵汤浇料融合得妙不可言；至于南瓜——天啊，馅料在舌头上感觉如此绵密！ “很特别，但我喜欢。腌鲱鱼怎么样？” 格里马尔德夹起一片黏稠的鱼肉。“我有点怪。我不喜欢鲱鱼，也不喜欢李子酱，但配李子酱的腌鲱鱼我可以吃上一整天。这里有太多好吃的了——虽然比不上一年一度的集市，但每个人都能找到喜欢的东西。” “一年一度的集市？” 他点点头。“是啊。以前，大部落会在那段时间来到艾尔斯泰德，大规模交易各自的货物；现在则变成了一场大型庆典，有游戏、表演，还有许多精致的进口商品。我小时候，家里会摆一个小摊，卖自制安纳泰饼干。爸爸现在还会做，只是比过去少多了。他曾在自己的故乡卡菲斯特学习当面包师，但不知为什么，一年后就退学了。要是你喜欢糕点，我可以给你弄些他最拿手的，刚出炉的那种。” “你吃了好多。得做大量运动才能全消耗掉，”你调侃道。 半安纳泰人坏笑起来。“那你有什么想法？” “不知道。也许我们可以去滑冰或滑雪，除非你更喜欢徒步？” 格里马尔德笑了。“我姐姐才是板类运动专家。我更擅长驾驶。” “你更喜欢开什么？喷气摩托？雪地摩托？飞行器？” “只要速度快，我都喜欢。去年我买了一辆老旧的IOTA-J悬浮摩托，稍微改造了一下。没什么花哨的：就是更换反重力线圈，再给喷气引擎装上更坚固的叶片。我更喜欢飞船，不过很少有机会驾驶。最容易接触到的是风暴卫士医疗穿梭机，那家伙可带劲了！” 你皱起眉头，啜了一口饮料。“真的？我还以为那是老型号？” 火热的伪娘点点头。“确实。它不是我们最老的飞行器，但总能完成任务。机身有点笨重，操纵也很生硬，不过只要掌握驾驶方法，就没有什么能拦住它。暴风雪、雷暴、电磁异常、巨型海怪，没有任何东西能折断它的翅膀或让引擎窒息。” 等等，巨型海怪？乌维托上有海怪？ “按照老卫兵的说法，是有的。我还没见过，但每次海上救援都会格外小心。银背鲨和尖刺龟已经够我们操心了，更别说冰冷潮汐。老救援队员讲过的一些故事会让人不寒而栗——我说真的。住在冰冻卫星上，还能让你冒冷汗的东西一定格外可怕。” “你是在拿我的[pc.isNaga |蛇身 |腿 ]开玩笑，对吧？” 顽皮的鸟儿咯咯笑了。“也许吧。还想再来一杯吗？” 你尝了些姜饼和饼干，又喝了一大口。“不了，我够了。天啊，我吃得好撑。” “我也是。你想——” [flags.GRIMALD_HANGOUT |“格里马尔德！[pc.name]！很高兴在这里见到你们，[pc.mf |小伙子们 |朋友们 ]！” |“嘿，伙计们，是格里马尔德！”一个魁梧的米洛丹人大喊。 “你认识他们？”你问。 格里马尔德点点头。“是的。他们是我的队友：乌瑟、奥维尔和埃尔达，”他说着，依次指向那只大猫、一个魁梧的熊变体人，以及一名亚马逊般的鹿变体人。” ] “天啊，他们俩依偎在一起好可爱！”埃尔达醉醺醺地咯咯笑道。 毛茸茸的熊紧紧看护着醉酒同伴。“我们正要去营房参加一次团队建设活动。你要和我们一起来吗？如果你的朋友愿意，[pc.heShe]也可以来！” “团队建设活动？”你问道[silly |，仿佛自己就是索利德·斯内克本人 ]。 “嗑药乱交，”格里马尔德解释。“我们只能自己找乐子。” 乌瑟把队友们搂进怀里。“所以，你到底来不来？我们可以一起干这个甜美的营房小鸟。” “或者说，你可以和我一起吸好多根鸡巴，”埃尔达补充道。“[pc.hasCock |我敢肯定你的尝起来像美梦一样 |我已经很久很久没尝过[pc.vagAss |硕大多汁的芒果 |硕大弹润的臀瓣 ] ]了。”
rows.raw: " “You wanna get a drink?” Grimald cocks an eyebrow. “I already have one, silly.” [silly |Smartass. |[pc.isBimbo |Well duh! |Stars, is he that oblivious? ] ] “I meant taking a drink TOGETHER.” The fiery femboy blushes. “H-Ha! Y-Y Ye... Yes, of course, I’d like that – definitely didn’t miss the obvious signal,” he babbles. He bashfully reaches for his radio transmitter. “Grimald here, do you read?” His device stays silent for long, pregnant seconds. “Grimald? You still workin’, boy?” “Y-Yes Fredholm. I-” “If you don’ clock out now I’m tellin’ yer Mom yer doing overtime again! Go have fun kiddo, that’s an order!” The feed suddenly cuts. Seems like he’s got the [dayNight |day |night ] off. “[flags.GRIMALD_HANGOUT |Fredholm’s really looking out for you, isn’t he?” Grimald nods. “Yeah. We better go else I’ll get a serious scolding. |Who’s that Fredholm fellow?” Grimald sighs. “The chief medical officer. My mother and him are like siblings, so I better get going. ]” You take him by the hand and tug him to downtown Irestead. The downy boy takes back the lead a moment later, guiding you through narrow streets, avoiding the most crowded places. In the blink of an eye, you reach the main crossroads. The cool winds blow hard but it’s not enough to discourage people from hanging around the many food and drink stalls. Spiced wines, hot chocolates, fizzy drinks, and exotic cocktails whisper sweet nothings to your ears while glazed treats and warm, greasy meats aggressively seduce your eyes. Everything looks so tasty! “What would you like? Something classic or a local specialty?” You lean closer. “Surprise me.” He smiles. “It’s gonna be a very sweet one, believe me. I’ll wait in line — would you kindly find us a seat near the fire?” The biting frost batters your face. Yes, you’ll do that. You don’t feel like waiting in the cold to[dayNight |day |night ]. Fortunately, the locals installed hardlight bowers and braziers along the buildings and near the food joints. You slowly walk through the scarce crowd in search of a free spot. [dayNight |Small children play in the snow, watched from afar by their parents. Tiny korgonne and huskars build snowmen with the help of young toves and a handful of essyra. The little ones sculpt big ears and large snouts into their snowy pieces, defying the laws of nature themselves to create silly chimeras and mythical creatures with their small hands. It must be nice to have snow all year long. |Ethereal colors dance in the sky, illuminating the snowy town with viridian lights. One, then two, then three auroras fill your eyes with shades of fuschia, purple, emerald, and amber. A few couples take advantage of the mesmerizing spectacle to make out and grope each other, cyborgs and avians in particular. Maybe auroras interfere with their circuits and psyche? ] You slowly relax, charmed by the arctic city. The insidious cold forces you to stay close to the blazing hotspots but overall, you could stay here for hours. Maybe you could buy a house here, for the holidays? There’s even a Steele Tech outpost nearby, if there’s an emergency and Anyx is close by too if you need some company. Speaking of company, Grimald’s been away for some time now. You hope he’s okay. “[pc.name]? A-A little help?” You look behind you. Grimald gives you an uneasy smile. The poor boy carries two drinks and a barrowful of steamy goods in his augmented hands. You can see the tiny pistons staining to keep them clenched. Feeling merciful[pc.isAss | for once ], you take one glass and an overflowing tray from him and place them on a nearby table. Your ambitious date slowly puts his drink down and carefully unpacks all the meats and sweets he got you. “Stars, that’s too much! It must have cost you a fortune!” The cocky bird smirks. “I got a discount – half the vendors here used to be my classmates. I got us pickled herring with plum-cranberry sauce, zhor beast meatballs with melted cheese, mashed potatoes with gravy and cheese, our homemade polar buns stuffed with onions, pickled cabbage, and seal bacon, stakh’how gumbo with eel pate, stuffed squash, steamed carrots and beans, and [silly |sweet rolls |honey gingerbread ].[flags.GRIMALD_HANGOUT | | I didn’t know if you were vegetarian, so I took a lot of extras. ]” “Everything smells so good. And what are we drinking?” you ask. “[rand |Spiced wine with milodan nutmeg! Don’t worry, all the alcohol has evaporated already so it’s safe to drink. |Reindeer dry! It’s a soft drink made with imported Tove fruits. The taste is very special but it goes with everything. |Irestead coffee! It’s ausar coffee with a pumpkin syrup base, whipped cream and torrefied squash beans on top. My Dad absolutely loves it, especially if it’s piping hot. |Stormguard mead! The recipe was made by the first Stormguards and the indigenous envoys when they sealed the first environment and traditions respect act. To this day, we still seal peace and trade treaties with a shared glass of mead. ] Cheers!” “Cheers!” You take a few sips before digging into the juicy food. There’s so many things to eat, so many flavors to explore! You try to keep it balanced, not too fat nor too light, just like Briget taught you. Grimald devours his buns and skewer, filling his mouth with greasy meats and cheese-covered potatoes. The half-anat stops when he sees you staring. “S-Sorry about that. We had an emergency earlier and I had to skip dinner. Did you try the stakh’hov gumbo? It’s a little crustacean that feeds on carrion and leftover meat stuck between the teeth of deep sea creatures. I know it doesn’t sound appealing, but it’s a real treat, especially with stuffed squash!” Not reassured the slightest, you pick some sauce-soaked meat and take a bite. He didn’t lie, it’s very tasty! The shrimp-like food has a surprisingly sour taste but it mixes heavenly with the gumbo topping, and the squash – stars, the stuffing feels so creamy on your tongue! “It’s special, but I like it. How’s the pickled herring?” Grimald takes a sticky slice of fish. “I’m a bit weird. I don’t like herring, I don’t like the plum sauce either, but I could eat pickled herring with plum sauce all day. There’s so many good things to eat – not as much as during the yearly fair but there’s stuff for everyone.” “The yearly fair?” He nods. “Yes. Back in the day, it was the period of time where the big tribes came to Irestead to mass trade their wares, but now it’s a big festival with games, spectacles, and lots of fancy imported goods. When I was a kid, my family held a small stall where we sold homemade anat cookies. Dad still makes some but a lot less than he used to. He studied to be a baker back on Caphist, his homeworld, but he dropped out after one year for some reason. If you like pastries, I can get you some of his best stuff, fresh from the oven.” “You’re eating a lot. You’ll need to do lots of exercise to burn it all down,” you tease. The half-anat smirks. “And what do you have in mind?” “I don’t know. Maybe we could go ice skating or skiing, unless you like hiking more?” Grimald smiles. “My sister’s the board sports expert. I’m more of a pilot.” “What do you prefer to drive? Jetbikes? Snowmobiles? Aircrafts?” “I like anything that goes fast. Last year, I bought an old IOTA-J hoverbike and gave it a little makeover. Nothing fancy: replacing the antigrav coils and installing sturdier blades to the jet engine. I prefer spaceships, but I don’t get to pilot them often. The closest I have access to is the Stormguard medical shuttle and this one rocks!” You frown, sipping on your drink. “Really? I thought it was an old model?” The fiery femboy nods. “Indeed. It’s not our oldest flyer but it gets things done. The fuselage is a bit bulky and the commands are rough but once you know how to steer it, nothing can stop you. Blizzards, thunderstorms, electromagnetic anomalies, giant krakens, nothing can break its wings or choke the engines.” Wait, giant krakens? There’s sea monsters on Uveto? “According to the Old Guard, yes. Haven’t seen one yet, but I’m always careful when we have a seaborne rescue. Between the silverback sharks and spiky turtles, we’ve got enough things to worry about already, and that’s not taking the icy tides into account. Some stories told by the old rescuers are bone-chilling – and I mean it. When you live on a frozen moon, it takes something extra scary to give you cold sweats.” “You’re pulling my [pc.isNaga |coils |leg ] here, aren’t you?” The cheeky bird giggles. “Maybe. Do you want another drink?” You taste some gingerbread and cookies before taking another gulp. “No, I’m fine. Stars, I’m so full.” “Me too. What do yo-” [flags.GRIMALD_HANGOUT |“Grimald! [pc.name]! Nice seeing you here, [pc.mf |lads |friends ]!” |“Hoi lads, it’s Grimald!” a burly milodan shouts. “Do you know them?” you ask. Grimald nods. “Yes. They are my teammates: Uther, Orvil, and Erda,” he says, pointing at the big feline, a burly bearmorph, and an amazonian deermorph .” ] “Stars, they look so cute and cuddly together!” Erda drunkenly giggles. The fuzzy bear tightly watches over his inebriated comrade. “We were going to the barrack for a teambuilding session. You wanna come with us? Your friend can come too if [pc.heShe] wants!” “A teambuilding session?” you ask[silly |, as if you were Solid Snake himself ]. “An orgy with narcotics,” Grimald explains. “We find our fun where we can.” Uther snuggles his teammates against him. “So, are you coming or nah? We can top this sweet barrack birdy together.” “Or like, you can suck lotsa dicks with me,” Erda adds. “[pc.hasCock |I’m sure yours tastes like a dream |I haven’t tasted [pc.vagAss |a big, juicy mango |big, bouncy buns ] in a long long time ].” "

[dayNight |It’s gonna be a long and hot and sweaty day |The night’s gonna be long and hot an- ]” “I’ve got it. [flags.GRIMALD_ORGY |Your friends took a liking to me, and to you too |Your friends look fun and I’m a very hungry [pc.mf |boy |girl ] ].” Reassured, your date finishes his drink and slowly stands. He wraps his arm around your waist, tugging you against him. You place a soft kiss on his neck and wrap your arm around his hips, resting your hand on his plump rear. Erda whistles and Orvil cackles. “Heck yeah! Your friend’s got some spirit.” Uther shakes his head. “[flags.GRIMALD_ORGY |Alright, bad company, en route!” |What’s your name, [pc.mf |boy |cutie ]?” “[pc.name][pc.kmhbb |, don’t forget it, big boy |, but it’s [pc.mf |Master |Mistress ] to you, kitten |, but it’s [pc.mf |Master |Mistress ] to you, kitten |, don’t forget it kitty boy |, but it’s [pc.mf |Master |Mistress ] to you, kitty boy ].” The musclebound milodan frowns. He stays still for a couple of seconds before bursting into laughter. “I understand why Grimald took a liking to you. Alright, bad company, en route!” ] Without further ado, the Stormguards lead you back to the north of Irestead. You hold Grimald tight against you. The poor boy hisses and gasps as you mercilessly fondle his rear and audibly peck him. His chromed fingers play with your [pc.isTaur |sides |[pc.ass] ] as well, but they are far more gentle than yours — gentler but a lot more intense. He kneads your sensitive flesh, squeezing lurid whines out of you. His teammates aren’t doing better either. Erda fishes for Orvil’s crotch without any form of decency. rows.translation: “也许下次吧，”你微笑着回答。 “也好，”米洛丹人回答道。“格里马尔德，你最好别让这次机会溜走！” “可我想操他们！”埃尔达撅起嘴。 她那魁梧的队友把她扛到肩上，朝神殿走去，给你和格里马尔德留下些私人空间 — 好吧...至少是在熙熙攘攘的市中心所能拥有的那一点。格里马尔德的朋友们虽然可爱又迷人，却给不了你这只毛茸茸的阿纳特能给你的东西。 “你们在风暴卫士里玩得可真开心。我听说那是个古怪的教团，但没想到会是个古怪的性爱教团。” 你的约会对象咯咯一笑。“噢，小傻瓜，所有教团都是古怪的性爱教团 – 那些装作不是的，只是谎撒得太差。这在艾尔斯泰德是个公开的秘密，不过主动提起这事多少有些失礼。当然，年轻新兵和某些已经充分融入的成员有时会利用神殿里的本地人满足自己的放纵需求，不过我们会尽量保持克制、控制好尺度。黑房间里自愿成年人之间发生的事，就留在黑房间里。” “你们还有别的好玩设备吗？” 格里马尔德想了一会儿。“本地还有一间桑拿房。它不属于风暴卫士，不过我们在那里租了几个房间，主要供长老使用，也用于公务。” 公务是什么意思？他们会在这里组织会议吗？ “不是啦，小傻瓜！条约签订后邀请人们去蒸桑拿是传统。伏特加可喝可不喝，但出一身汗，再跳进冰冷的水里则必不可少。起初，本地原住民领袖还以为这是一种萨满仪式，要把协议烙进签署者的灵魂深处，以此让它牢不可破。” “想和我一起去蒸桑拿吗？气氛很快就会变得热气腾腾，尤其是在一只娇嫩的阿纳特与他的[pc.race][flags.GRIMALD_SEX |炮友 |朋友 ]之间。” 热情似火的伪娘。“我不怕浑身湿透、汗流浃背，可要我一头扎进冷水池...还是算了吧。别误会，我很乐意赤身裸体和你待在一个又热又湿的房间里，不过像现在这样肚子里装满丰盛食物和软饮料，我会更开心。” 他说得没错。星辰在上，你实在太饱了。享用完这场小盛宴后，你觉得自己什么也做不了。走回神殿都会是一场挑战！ “要帮忙吗？”格里马尔德问。 “有人帮我一把，我当然不会反对。” 半阿纳特坏笑起来。“我知道该怎么让你像雪豹一样飞奔过雪地。” 格里马尔德化作一道残影！这只调皮的鸟儿用掌心捧起新雪，转眼间便把它捏成一个圆滚滚的雪球！[pc.reflexesRange 40 |你险险躲过他的第一击！星辰在上，太悬了！ |雪球正中你的胸口，把你的正面打成一片湿漉漉的雪白。 ] “格里马尔德！你这个小...混蛋！我要让你吃不了兜着走！” “来一个又凶又大的吻？”他撅起嘴，狡黠地调戏道。 既然他想玩这个游戏，那你就陪他玩到底！你飞快[pc.isNaga |滑向 |跑向 ]附近的一堆积雪，把双手插进纯净的雪中。眨眼间，你便捏出一把冰冷的投射物，开始瞄准。[pc.aimRange 40 |你以一条低矮的弧线掷出第一个雪球！雪球击中了格里马尔德的左肩！ “现在没那么嚣张了吧？” |你把第一个雪球笔直地掷出去！格里马尔德在最后一刻低头躲开 — 可恶，差点就打中他了！ ] 义体护士咯咯笑起来。“这才叫玩嘛！来吧，[pc.name]，让我看看你有多大本事！” [silly |街道化作无人区，路人们全都吓得缩成一团 |宛如暴雨般的雪球倾泻在街道上 ]！你俯身躲闪，又跃出视线，避开一发发越来越接近目标的弹丸！格里马尔德的准头杀气十足，要不是你在冒险中磨练出的反应速度，你早已变成一尊冰冷的雪[pc.mf |人 |女 ]，或者一个雪[pc.isAss |魔 |天使 ]了。他发射和装填的速度极快，几乎不给你调整火力或把雪球捏成规整形状的时间。 战斗十分艰苦，但你的父母可没养出一个轻言放弃的人！你的投掷次数或许没他多，但雪球飞得和他的一样远、一样快。格里马尔德以杂技般的动作旋身闪开，几乎像一位毛茸茸的芭蕾舞者般在雪地上起舞。他左右跳跃、猛扑，扭动躯干，放肆地甩动臀部，违背物理定律般躲过你一次次大胆的攻击。对他而言，这一切看上去如此轻松、如此自然。 “以一个外星人来说，挺不错嘛，”他躲在路灯柱后高声喊道。“再这样下去，你可要让我出汗了！” 你坏笑起来。“我还没收拾完你呢，坏男孩。” 既然数量解决不了问题，你就专注于质量。你竭尽所能避开他的攻击，利用能找到的那一点点掩体，捏出又大又圆的雪球。每做好一个，你就瞄准格里马尔德。羽毛覆盖的风暴卫士继续跳出射程，但你更快、更有力的弹丸逐渐把他的运动能力逼到极限。他的动作变得凌乱而飘忽，胸膛起伏得越来越快，呼吸沉重 – 他撑不了多久了！ “吃我这招！”你大喊着掷出一记凶狠的曲线球。 格里马尔德险险躲开！星辰在上，就差一点！半阿纳特坏笑起来。“现在轮到我了！”
rows.raw: " “Maybe another time,” you answer with a smile. “Fair enough,” the milodan replies. “You better not let this one slide, Grimald!” “But I wanted to fuck them!” Erda pouts. Her burly teammate lifts her over his shoulder before heading to the temple, leaving Grimald and you some privacy — well... as much as one can have in a crowded downtown. As lovely and charming as Grimald’s friends are, they can’t offer you what the fluffy anat can. “You guys are having lots of fun in the Stormguard. I heard that it was a weird cult, but I didn’t expect it to be a weird sex cult.” Your date giggles. “Oh silly, all cults are weird sex cults – and those that pretend otherwise lie badly. It’s an open secret around Irestead, but it’s kind of a faux pas to raise the issue. Sure, the young recruits and some well-integrated members sometimes use the temple’s locals for their self-indulgent needs but we try to keep it tame and in control. What happens between consenting adults in the black room stays in the black room.” “Do you have other fun appliances?” Grimald thinks for a moment. “There’s the local sauna. The Stormguard doesn’t own it but we rent a couple of rooms there, mostly for the elders and for business purposes.” What does he mean for business purposes? Do they organize meetings here? “No silly! It’s tradition to invite people to the sauna after sealing a treaty. Vodka is optional but sweating and taking a dip in ice cold water isn’t. At first, the local indigenous leaders thought it was a kind of shamanic ritual to toughen the deal by branding it into the signatories’ very souls.” “Wanna hit the sauna with me? Things could get steamy very quickly, especially between a tender anat and his [pc.race] [flags.GRIMALD_SEX |fuckbuddy |friend ].” The fiery femboy. “I’m not afraid of getting wet and sweaty, but diving head first into the cold pool... no thanks. Don’t get me wrong, I’d love to hang around with you in my birthday suit in a hot and wet room, but I’m happier like this, with a belly full of rich food and soft drinks.” He’s not wrong. Stars, you are so full. You don’t think you can do anything after your little feast. Walking back to the temple will be a challenge! “Need a hand?” Grimald asks. “I wouldn’t be against a little help.” The half-anat smirks. “I know exactly how to make you run through the snow like a snow panther.” Grimald moves in a blur! The cheeky bird samples fresh snow in his palm, molding it into a round snowball in a heartbeat! [pc.reflexesRange 40 |You narrowly dodge his first hit! Stars, that was close! |He hits you square in the chest, turning your front into a white, wet mess. ] “Grimald! You lil’... brat! You won’t know what hit you!” “A big, mean kiss?” he wryly teases, puckering his lips. If he wants to play this game, then you’re gonna play it! You quickly [pc.isNaga |slide |run ] toward a nearby pile of snow and plunge both hands into the pristine material. In the blink of an eye, you create a handful of ice projectiles and take aim. [pc.aimRange 40 |You fire the first ball with a low curve! The snowball hits Grimald’s left shoulder! “Not so cocky anymore, aren’t you?” |You fire the first snowball in a straight line! Grimald ducks at the last moment — dang, you almost got him! ] The cyborg nurse giggles. “Now we’re playing! Come [pc.name], show me what you are made of!” [silly |Passersby cower in fear as the streets turn into a no man’s land |A proverbial shower of snowballs rain down the streets ]! You crouch and leap out of sight, evading bullets that come closer and closer to hitting you! Grimald’s got a killer aim, if it weren’t for your adventure-honed reflexes, you’d already be a chilly snow[pc.mf |man |woman ], or a snow [pc.isAss |demon |angel ]. He fires and reloads quickly, barely leaving you any time to adjust your fire or build your balls into a proper shape. The battle’s hard but your parents raised no quitter! You might not shoot as many times as he does, but your snowballs fly as far and as fast as his. Grimald acrobatically swirls out of reach, almost dancing on the snow like a fluffy ballerina. He hops and pounces left and right, twisting his torso and throwing his hips around indecently, defying the laws of physics to avoid your daring attacks. It looks so easy, so natural for him. “Not bad for an offworlder,” he shouts from behind a lamppost. “If you keep going on like this, you’re gonna make me break a sweat!” You smirk. “I’m not finished with you, bad boy.” If quantity doesn’t do it, you’ll focus on quality. You avoid his attacks the best you can, using what little cover you can find to make big, round spheres. As soon as one’s ready, you aim it at Grimald. The feathered stormguard continues to bounce out of range but your faster, stronger bullets push his athletic prowess to their limits. His moves are more ragged, more erratic, his chest rises faster and faster, breathing heavily – he won’t last much longer! “Take that!” you scream, throwing a mean curve ball. Grimald narrowly dodges it! Stars, you were so close! The half-anat smirks. “My turn now!” "
